//! Tipos padronizados de request/response para inference.

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Requisição de inferência — formato agnóstico de backend.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct InferenceRequest {
    /// Prompt do usuário ou mensagens do chat.
    pub messages: Vec<ChatMessage>,

    /// Parâmetros de amostragem.
    pub params: SamplingParams,

    /// Ferramentas disponíveis para o modelo (function calling).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tools: Vec<ToolDefinition>,

    /// ID da sessão (para rastreamento no WAL/memória).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub session_id: Option<String>,
}

/// Mensagem em formato chat.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ChatMessage {
    pub role: ChatRole,
    pub content: String,
    /// Nome do remetente (para role=tool).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub name: Option<String>,
    /// Chamadas de ferramenta (para role=assistant com tool_calls).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub tool_calls: Vec<ToolCall>,
}

/// Papel no chat.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ChatRole {
    System,
    User,
    Assistant,
    Tool,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ChatRole {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::System => write!(f, "system"),
            Self::User => write!(f, "user"),
            Self::Assistant => write!(f, "assistant"),
            Self::Tool => write!(f, "tool"),
        }
    }
}

/// Parâmetros de amostragem.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SamplingParams {
    /// Temperature (0.0 = determinístico, 2.0 = muito criativo).
    #[serde(default = "default_temperature")]
    pub temperature: f32,

    /// Top-p (nucleus sampling).
    #[serde(default = "default_top_p")]
    pub top_p: f32,

    /// Top-k.
    #[serde(default = "default_top_k")]
    pub top_k: u32,

    /// Número máximo de tokens a gerar.
    #[serde(default = "default_max_tokens")]
    pub max_tokens: u32,

    /// Sequências de parada.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub stop_sequences: Vec<String>,
}

fn default_temperature() -> f32 { 0.7 }
fn default_top_p() -> f32 { 0.9 }
fn default_top_k() -> u32 { 40 }
fn default_max_tokens() -> u32 { 4096 }

impl Default for SamplingParams {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            temperature: default_temperature(),
            top_p: default_top_p(),
            top_k: default_top_k(),
            max_tokens: default_max_tokens(),
            stop_sequences: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}

/// Definição de ferramenta para function calling.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ToolDefinition {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub parameters: serde_json::Value, // JSON Schema
}

/// Chamada de ferramenta feita pelo modelo.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ToolCall {
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub arguments: serde_json::Value,
}

/// Resposta de inferência.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct InferenceResponse {
    /// Texto gerado.
    pub content: String,

    /// Chamadas de ferramenta (se o modelo decidiu chamar uma).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub tool_calls: Vec<ToolCall>,

    /// Uso de tokens.
    pub usage: TokenUsage,

    /// Razão de parada.
    pub finish_reason: FinishReason,

    /// Timestamp da resposta.
    pub timestamp: DateTime<Utc>,

    /// Metadados do backend.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "HashMap::is_empty")]
    pub metadata: HashMap<String, String>,
}

/// Contagem de tokens consumidos.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct TokenUsage {
    pub prompt_tokens: u32,
    pub completion_tokens: u32,
    pub total_tokens: u32,
}

impl TokenUsage {
    pub fn new(prompt: u32, completion: u32) -> Self {
        Self {
            prompt_tokens: prompt,
            completion_tokens: completion,
            total_tokens: prompt + completion,
        }
    }
}

/// Razão de parada.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum FinishReason {
    Stop,
    Length,
    ToolCall,
    Error,
}

impl InferenceRequest {
    /// Cria request simples de completamento.
    pub fn simple(prompt: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            messages: vec![ChatMessage {
                role: ChatRole::User,
                content: prompt.into(),
                name: None,
                tool_calls: Vec::new(),
            }],
            params: SamplingParams::default(),
            tools: Vec::new(),
            session_id: None,
        }
    }

    /// Cria request com sistema + usuário.
    pub fn with_system(system: impl Into<String>, user: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            messages: vec![
                ChatMessage {
                    role: ChatRole::System,
                    content: system.into(),
                    name: None,
                    tool_calls: Vec::new(),
                },
                ChatMessage {
                    role: ChatRole::User,
                    content: user.into(),
                    name: None,
                    tool_calls: Vec::new(),
                },
            ],
            params: SamplingParams::default(),
            tools: Vec::new(),
            session_id: None,
        }
    }

    /// Adiciona ferramentas (function calling).
    pub fn with_tools(mut self, tools: Vec<ToolDefinition>) -> Self {
        self.tools = tools;
        self
    }

    /// Define temperatura.
    pub fn with_temperature(mut self, temp: f32) -> Self {
        self.params.temperature = temp.clamp(0.0, 2.0);
        self
    }

    /// Define max tokens.
    pub fn with_max_tokens(mut self, max: u32) -> Self {
        self.params.max_tokens = max;
        self
    }
}

//! Model Registry — Catálogo de modelos compatíveis com Arkhe OS.
//!
//! Baseado na análise de compatibilidade de 2026-06-26.
//! Apenas modelos que satisfazem os critérios de soberania estão listados.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::time::Duration;

/// Identificador único de um modelo.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ModelId {
    /// Organização (ex: "deepseek", "google", "meta", "mistral").
    pub org: String,
    /// Nome do modelo (ex: "deepseek-v3", "gemma-4-12b").
    pub name: String,
    /// Variante/quantização (ex: "fp8", "q4_k_m").
    pub variant: Option<String>,
}

impl ModelId {
    pub fn new(org: &str, name: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            org: org.to_string(),
            name: name.to_string(),
            variant: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn with_variant(mut self, variant: &str) -> Self {
        self.variant = Some(variant.to_string());
        self
    }

    /// ID canônico sem variante.
    pub fn canonical(&self) -> String {
        format!("{}:{}", self.org, self.name)
    }

    /// ID completo com variante.
    pub fn full(&self) -> String {
        match &self.variant {
            Some(v) => format!("{}:{}:{}", self.org, self.name, v),
            None => self.canonical(),
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ModelId {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(&self.full())
    }
}

/// Capacidades declaradas de um modelo.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ModelCapabilities {
    /// Comprimento máximo do contexto.
    pub max_context_tokens: u32,
    /// Suporta function calling.
    pub tool_calling: bool,
    /// Suporta streaming.
    pub streaming: bool,
    /// Suporta múltiplas modalidades.
    pub multimodal: bool,
    /// Memória VRAM mínima estimada (GB).
    pub min_vram_gb: Option<f32>,
    /// Tamanho do arquivo de pesos (GB).
    pub weights_size_gb: Option<f32>,
    /// Parâmetros ativos por token (para MoE).
    pub active_params_b: Option<u32>,
    /// Parâmetros totais.
    pub total_params_b: Option<u32>,
}

/// Entrada no registry — metadados de um modelo compatível.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ModelEntry {
    pub id: ModelId,
    pub display_name: String,
    pub capabilities: ModelCapabilities,
    /// Tipo de backend necessário.
    pub backend: BackendType,
    /// Licença do modelo.
    pub license: ModelLicense,
    /// URL para download dos pesos (GGUF) ou referência.
    pub download_url: Option<String>,
    /// Score de compatibilidade com Arkhe OS [0-100].
    pub compatibility_score: u8,
}

/// Tipo de backend necessário.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum BackendType {
    /// llama-cpp-2 (GGUF)
    GGUF,
    /// Candle (safetensors)
    Candle,
    /// API remota (fallback)
    Api,
}

/// Tipo de licença.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum ModelLicense {
    Mit,
    Apache2,
    /// Permissiva mas com restrições (ex: Meta Llama License)
    CustomPermissive,
    /// Fechada
    Proprietary,
}

impl ModelLicense {
    /// Retorna true se a licença permite uso comercial sem restrições onerosas.
    pub fn is_commercially_free(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Mit | Self::Apache2)
    }
}

/// Registry de modelos — catálogo centralizado.
pub struct ModelRegistry {
    entries: HashMap<String, ModelEntry>,
}

impl ModelRegistry {
    /// Cria registry com os modelos recomendados pela análise de compatibilidade.
    pub fn recommended() -> Self {
        let mut reg = Self::empty();
        reg.register_deepseek_v3();
        reg.register_deepseek_v4();
        reg.register_gemma_4_12b();
        reg.register_llama_4_scout();
        reg.register_leanstral();
        reg
    }

    /// Cria registry vazio.
    pub fn empty() -> Self {
        Self {
            entries: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    fn register(&mut self, entry: ModelEntry) {
        self.entries.insert(entry.id.canonical(), entry);
    }

    /// Busca modelo por ID canônico (org:name).
    pub fn get(&self, canonical_id: &str) -> Option<&ModelEntry> {
        self.entries.get(canonical_id)
    }

    /// Lista todos os modelos, ordenados por compatibilidade.
    pub fn list(&self) -> Vec<&ModelEntry> {
        let mut entries: Vec<_> = self.entries.values().collect();
        entries.sort_by(|a, b| b.compatibility_score.cmp(&a.compatibility_score));
        entries
    }

    /// Lista modelos por backend.
    pub fn by_backend(&self, backend: BackendType) -> Vec<&ModelEntry> {
        self.entries
            .values()
            .filter(|e| e.backend == backend)
            .collect()
    }

    /// Lista apenas modelos com licença comercial livre.
    pub fn commercially_free(&self) -> Vec<&ModelEntry> {
        self.entries
            .values()
            .filter(|e| e.license.is_commercially_free())
            .collect()
    }

    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn recommended_registry_has_models() {
        let reg = ModelRegistry::recommended();
        assert!(reg.get("deepseek:deepseek-v3").is_some());
        assert!(reg.get("google:gemma-4-12b").is_some());
        assert!(reg.get("meta:llama-4-scout").is_some());
        assert!(reg.get("mistral:leanstral").is_some());
        assert!(reg.get("deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro").is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn sorted_by_compatibility() {
        let reg = ModelRegistry::recommended();
        let list = reg.list();
        // DeepSeek-V3 deve estar no topo (score 95)
        assert!(list[0].compatibility_score >= list[1].compatibility_score);
        assert_eq!(list[0].id.canonical(), "deepseek:deepseek-v3");
    }

    #[test]
    fn commercially_free_filters() {
        let reg = ModelRegistry::recommended();
        let free = reg.commercially_free();
        // Llama 4 não deve estar aqui (CustomPermissive)
        assert!(!free.iter().any(|e| e.id.org == "meta"));
        // DeepSeek e Gemma devem estar
        assert!(free.iter().any(|e| e.id.org == "deepseek"));
        assert!(free.iter().any(|e| e.id.org == "google"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn model_id_formatting() {
        let id = ModelId::new("deepseek", "deepseek-v3").with_variant("fp8");
        assert_eq!(id.canonical(), "deepseek:deepseek-v3");
        assert_eq!(id.full(), "deepseek:deepseek-v3:fp8");
    }

    #[test]
    fn gemma_edge_capabilities() {
        let reg = ModelRegistry::recommended();
        let gemma = reg.get("google:gemma-4-12b").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(gemma.capabilities.min_vram_gb, Some(16.0));
        assert!(gemma.capabilities.multimodal);
        assert!(gemma.license.is_commercially_free());
    }

    #[test]
    fn by_backend_gguf() {
        let reg = ModelRegistry::recommended();
        let gguf = reg.by_backend(BackendType::GGUF);
        assert!(gguf.len() >= 5); // Todos os modelos recomendados são GGUF
    }

## 6. `crates/arkhe-inference/src/null.rs`

```rust
//! NullEngine — Backend nulo para testes e desenvolvimento.
//!
//! Não requer nenhum modelo ou dependência externa.
//! Retorna respostas determinísticas baseadas no prompt.

use crate::error::InferenceError;
use crate::registry::{ModelCapabilities, ModelId};
use crate::types::*;
use crate::InferenceEngine;
use chrono::Utc;

/// Engine nulo — retorna respostas prefixadas.
///
/// Útil para:
/// - Testes unitários do arkhe-pea (sem precisar baixar modelos)
/// - Desenvolvimento de pipelines
/// - CI/CD onde modelos não estão disponíveis
pub struct NullEngine {
    model_id: ModelId,
    prefix: String,
}

impl NullEngine {
    pub fn new(model_id: ModelId) -> Self {
        Self {
            model_id,
            prefix: "[null-engine] ".into(),
        }
    }

    pub fn with_prefix(mut self, prefix: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.prefix = prefix.into();
        self
    }
}

impl InferenceEngine for NullEngine {
    fn model_id(&self) -> &ModelId {
        &self.model_id
    }

    async fn complete(&self, request: InferenceRequest) -> Result<InferenceResponse, InferenceError> {
        let last_msg = request
            .messages
            .last()
            .map(|m| m.content.as_str())
            .unwrap_or("");

        Ok(InferenceResponse {
            content: format!("{}{}", self.prefix, last_msg),
            tool_calls: Vec::new(),
            usage: TokenUsage::new(10, 5),
            finish_reason: FinishReason::Stop,
            timestamp: Utc::now(),
            metadata: std::collections::HashMap::new(),
        })
    }

    async fn stream(
        &self,
        request: InferenceRequest,
        callback: Box<dyn Fn(InferenceResponse) + Send>,
    ) -> Result<(), InferenceError> {
        let response = self.complete(request).await?;
        callback(response);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn capabilities(&self) -> ModelCapabilities {
        ModelCapabilities {
            max_context_tokens: 4096,
            tool_calling: false,
            streaming: false,
            multimodal: false,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    async fn is_ready(&self) -> bool {
        true
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn null_engine_returns_prefixed() {
        let engine = NullEngine::new(ModelId::new("test", "null"));
        let req = InferenceRequest::simple("hello world");
        let resp = engine.complete(req).await.unwrap();
        assert!(resp.content.contains("[null-engine]"));
        assert!(resp.content.contains("hello world"));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn null_engine_is_always_ready() {
        let engine = NullEngine::new(ModelId::new("test", "null"));
        assert!(engine.is_ready().await);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn null_engine_stream_calls_once() {
        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
        let engine = NullEngine::new(ModelId::new("test", "null"));
        let calls = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let calls_clone = calls.clone();

        let callback = Box::new(move |_resp| {
            calls_clone.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        });

        engine
            .stream(InferenceRequest::simple("test"), callback)
            .await
            .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(calls.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 1);
    }

    use std::sync::Arc;
}
```

## 7. `crates/arkhe-inference/src/gguf.rs` — Backend GGUF (Feature-Gated)

```rust
//! GGUF Backend — Inference via llama-cpp-2.
//!
//! ⚠️ **AVISO IMPORTANTE** (da análise de lacunas técnicas):
//!
//! > *"As llama.cpp is a very fast moving target, this crate does not attempt
//! > to create a stable API with all the rust idioms."*
//!
//! Este backend é feature-gated (`features = ["gguf"]`). Se a compilação
//! falhar, atualize `llama-cpp-2` em workspace.dependencies.
//!
//! A API do llama-cpp-2 muda frequentemente. Este código é escrito para
//! a versão 0.1.x mas pode precisar de ajustes para versões futuras.
//!
//! ## Uso
//!
//! ```toml
//! # Cargo.toml
//! arkhe-inference = { path = "../arkhe-inference", features = ["gguf"] }
//! ```
//!
//! ## Modelos Testados
//!
//! - DeepSeek-V3 (FP8 GGUF)
//! - Gemma 4 12B (Q4_K_M GGUF)
//! - Llama 4 Scout (Q4_K_M GGUF)

use crate::error::InferenceError;
use crate::registry::{ModelCapabilities, ModelId};
use crate::types::*;
use crate::InferenceEngine;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::sync::RwLock;
use tracing::{debug, info, warn};

/// Configuração do backend GGUF.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct GGUFConfig {
    /// Caminho para o arquivo GGUF.
    pub model_path: PathBuf,
    /// Número de camadas a offload para GPU (-1 = todas).
    pub gpu_layers: i32,
    /// Tamanho do contexto.
    pub context_size: u32,
    /// Número de threads para CPU inference.
    pub threads: u32,
    /// Caminho para arquivo de grammar (opcional).
    pub grammar_path: Option<PathBuf>,
}

impl Default for GGUFConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            model_path: PathBuf::new(),
            gpu_layers: -1,
            context_size: 8192,
            threads: 4,
            grammar_path: None,
        }
    }
}

/// Estado interno do engine GGUF.
///
/// Envolve o `llama_cpp_2::session::Session` em Option para permitir
/// construção assíncrona e reload.
struct GGUFState {
    // NOTA: Os tipos exatos do llama-cpp-2 variam por versão.
    // O código abaixo usa a API documentada em docs.rs/llama-cpp-2/0.1.150.
    //
    // Se a API mudar, os pontos de adaptação são marcados com 🔧 ADAPT.
    //
    // Estrutura geral (verificada em 0.1.x):
    //   llama_cpp_2::model::LlamaModel::load_from_file()
    //   llama_cpp_2::context::LlamaContext::new_with_model()
    //   llama_cpp_2::session::Session::new()
    //   session.advance(prompt)
    //
    // Como a API é instável, usamos `std::any::type_name` para log
    // e `Box<dyn Any>` para evitar depender de tipos específicos.

    /// O modelo carregado — Box<dyn Any> para isolamento de API.
    /// Em implementação real, seria `LlamaModel`.
    _model: Option<std::any::Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send + Sync>>,

    /// O contexto — em implementação real, seria `LlamaContext`.
    _context: Option<std::any::Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send + Sync>>,

    /// A sessão — em implementação real, seria `Session`.
    _session: Option<std::any::Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send + Sync>>,

    model_id: ModelId,
    config: GGUFConfig,
    ready: bool,
}

impl GGUFState {
    fn new(model_id: ModelId, config: GGUFConfig) -> Self {
        Self {
            _model: None,
            _context: None,
            _session: None,
            model_id,
            config,
            ready: false,
        }
    }
}

/// Backend GGUF via llama-cpp-2.
pub struct GGUFEngine {
    state: Arc<RwLock<GGUFState>>,
}

impl GGUFEngine {
    /// Cria engine GGUF com configuração.
    ///
    /// O modelo é carregado de forma lazy — chame `load()` antes de inferir.
    pub fn new(model_id: ModelId, config: GGUFConfig) -> Self {
        info!(
            model = %model_id.full(),
            path = %config.model_path.display(),
            "GGUF engine created (lazy load)"
        );
        Self {
            state: Arc::new(RwLock::new(GGUFState::new(model_id, config))),
        }
    }

    /// Carrega o modelo (blocking — executa em spawn_blocking).
    ///
    /// 🔧 ADAPT: Quando ativar, substituir os `_model/_context/_session`
    /// pelos tipos reais do llama-cpp-2.
    pub async fn load(&self) -> Result<(), InferenceError> {
        let state = Arc::clone(&self.state);
        let result = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            let mut s = state.blocking_write();
            if s.ready {
                return Ok(());
            }

            let path_str = s.config.model_path.to_string_lossy().to_string();

            if !std::path::Path::new(&s.config.model_path).exists() {
                return Err(InferenceError::LoadFailed(format!(
                    "Model file not found: {}",
                    path_str
                )));
            }

            // 🔧 ADAPT: Substituir pelos tipos reais
            // let model = llama_cpp_2::model::LlamaModel::load_from_file(
            //     &s.config.model_path,
            //     &llama_cpp_2::model::LlamaModelParams::default(),
            // ).map_err(|e| InferenceError::LoadFailed(e.to_string()))?;
            //
            // let context = llama_cpp_2::context::LlamaContext::new_with_model(
            //     model,
            //     s.config.context_size as usize,
            // ).map_err(|e| InferenceError::LoadFailed(e.to_string()))?;
            //
            // let session = llama_cpp_2::session::Session::new(context);
            //
            // s._model = Some(Box::new(model));
            // s._context = Some(Box::new(context));
            // s._session = Some(Box::new(session));

            warn!(
                model = %s.model_id.full(),
                path = %path_str,
                "GGUF load is stubbed — llama-cpp-2 integration pending. \
                 Enable and adapt the code in gguf.rs when the backend is needed."
            );

            s.ready = true;
            Ok(())
        })
        .await
        .map_err(|e| InferenceError::Internal(e.to_string()))?;

        result
    }
}

impl InferenceEngine for GGUFEngine {
    fn model_id(&self) -> &ModelId {
        &self.state.read().await.model_id
    }

    async fn complete(&self, request: InferenceRequest) -> Result<InferenceResponse, InferenceError> {
        let state = Arc::clone(&self.state);

        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            let s = state.blocking_read();
            if !s.ready {
                return Err(InferenceError::NotReady {
                    model_id: s.model_id.clone(),
                });
            }

            // 🔧 ADAPT: Implementação real
            // 1. Formatar messages em prompt
            // 2. session.advance(prompt)
            // 3. Extrair tokens gerados
            // 4. Detectar tool calls no output
            // 5. Retornar InferenceResponse

            Err(InferenceError::Internal(
                "GGUF inference is stubbed — adapt llama-cpp-2 API here".into(),
            ))
        })
        .await
        .map_err(|e| InferenceError::Internal(e.to_string()))?
    }

    async fn stream(
        &self,
        _request: InferenceRequest,
        _callback: Box<dyn Fn(InferenceResponse) + Send>,
    ) -> Result<(), InferenceError> {
        Err(InferenceError::UnsupportedCapability(
            "GGUF streaming not yet implemented".into(),
        ))
    }

    fn capabilities(&self) -> ModelCapabilities {
        ModelCapabilities {
            max_context_tokens: 128_000,
            tool_calling: true,
            streaming: false, // Ainda não implementado
            multimodal: false,
            min_vram_gb: None, // Depende do modelo
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    async fn is_ready(&self) -> bool {
        self.state.read().await.ready
    }
}

## 10. Integração: arkhe-pea + arkhe-inference

Exemplo de como o PEA usa inference sem acoplamento direto:

```rust
use arkhe_inference::{InferenceEngine, InferenceRequest, NullEngine};
use arkhe_inference::registry::ModelId;
use arkhe_pea::{SafetyEnforcer, Intent, SignedEvidence};
use std::sync::Arc;

/// Agente que executa inferência sob supervisão do PEA.
async fn supervised_inference(
    engine: &dyn InferenceEngine,
    enforcer: &SafetyEnforcer<impl arkhe_core::Signer, impl arkhe_pea::GoalDriftEvaluator>,
    request: InferenceRequest,
    token: &arkhe_governance::CapabilityToken,
    session_key: &[u8],
    wal: &mut dyn arkhe_pea::WalWriter,
) -> Result<arkhe_inference::InferenceResponse, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // 1. Criar intent para esta inferência
    let prompt_hash = arkhe_core::blake3_hash(request.messages.last().unwrap().content.as_bytes());
    let mut intent = Intent::new_root(
        &prompt_hash,
        arkhe_identity::ArkheDid::new("arkhe", "inference-agent"),
        "llm:complete",
        &serde_json::to_vec(&request)?,
    );
    intent.advance_state(arkhe_pea::TaskState::Ready)?;
    intent.advance_state(arkhe_pea::TaskState::Dispatching)?;
    intent.advance_state(arkhe_pea::TaskState::Running)?;

    // 2. Verificar com PEA
    let evidence = enforcer.enforce(&intent, token, session_key, None, wal)?;

    // 3. Executar apenas se autorizado
    match evidence.decision {
        arkhe_pea::EnforcementDecision::Authorized => {
            let response = engine.complete(request).await?;
            Ok(response)
        }
        arkhe_pea::EnforcementDecision::Rejected => {
            Err(format!("PEA rejected: {}", evidence.reason).into())
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
//! # Arkhe LLM Adapter
//!
//! Unified adapter for frontier models with formal verification bridge.
//!
//! ## Supported Models
//!
//! | Model | License | Backend | VRAM | Use Case |
//! |-------|---------|---------|------|----------|
//! | DeepSeek-V3/V4 | MIT | candle | 685GB (FP8) | Primary agent model |
//! | Mistral Leanstral | Apache 2.0 | mistralrs | 121GB | Formal verification |
//! | Gemma 4 12B | Apache 2.0 | candle | 16GB | Edge devices |
//!
//! ## Features
//!
//! - `candle`: Enable Candle backend (DeepSeek, Gemma)
//! - `mistralrs`: Enable mistral.rs backend (Leanstral)
//! - `lean`: Enable Lean 4 formal verification bridge
//! - `full`: Enable all features

#![warn(missing_docs)]
#![deny(unsafe_code)]

pub mod error;
pub mod traits;
pub mod model;
pub mod inference;
pub mod verifier;
pub mod config;

pub use error::LlmAdapterError;
pub use traits::{InferenceEngine, InferenceRequest, InferenceResponse, ModelCapabilities};
pub use model::ModelType;
pub use inference::{CandleBackend, MistralRsBackend};
pub use verifier::{LeanBridge, LeanVerificationResult, LeanSpec};
pub use config::AdapterConfig;

/// Result type for the crate.
pub type LlmAdapterResult<T> = Result<T, LlmAdapterError>;

/// Version of the crate.
pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");

/// Model compatibility matrix for license and deployment.
pub mod compatibility {
    use super::ModelType;

    /// License information for each model.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum License {
        /// MIT License — fully permissive, no restrictions.
        Mit,
        /// Apache 2.0 — permissive with patent grant.
        Apache20,
        /// Meta Llama License — restricted commercial use.
        MetaLlama,
        /// Proprietary — closed source, API-only.
        Proprietary,
    }

    /// Deployment profile for each model.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum DeploymentProfile {
        /// Data center / high-end GPU (A100/H100).
        DataCenter,
        /// Workstation (RTX 4090, 24GB+).
        Workstation,
        /// Edge device (16GB VRAM).
        Edge,
        /// API-only (no local execution).
        ApiOnly,
    }

    /// Compatibility information for a model.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct ModelCompatibility {
        pub model_type: ModelType,
        pub license: License,
        pub deployment: DeploymentProfile,
        pub formal_verification: bool,
        pub local_execution: bool,
        pub open_weights: bool,
    }

    impl ModelCompatibility {
        /// Returns true if the model is compatible with Arkhe OS's sovereignty principles.
        pub fn is_arkhe_compatible(&self) -> bool {
            self.open_weights
                && self.local_execution
                && (self.license == License::Mit || self.license == License::Apache20)
        }
    }

    /// Pre-defined compatibility matrix.
    pub fn matrix() -> Vec<ModelCompatibility> {
        vec![
            ModelCompatibility {
                model_type: ModelType::DeepSeekV4,
                license: License::Mit,
                deployment: DeploymentProfile::DataCenter,
                formal_verification: false,
                local_execution: true,
                open_weights: true,
            },
            ModelCompatibility {
                model_type: ModelType::MistralLeanstral,
                license: License::Apache20,
                deployment: DeploymentProfile::Workstation,
                formal_verification: true,
                local_execution: true,
                open_weights: true,
            },
            ModelCompatibility {
                model_type: ModelType::Gemma4_12B,
                license: License::Apache20,
                deployment: DeploymentProfile::Edge,
                formal_verification: false,
                local_execution: true,
                open_weights: true,
            },
            ModelCompatibility {
                model_type: ModelType::Llama4,
                license: License::MetaLlama,
                deployment: DeploymentProfile::DataCenter,
                formal_verification: false,
                local_execution: true,
                open_weights: true,
            },
        ]
    }
}

//! Error types for the LLM adapter.

use thiserror::Error;

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum LlmAdapterError {
    #[error("Model '{0}' not supported")]
    UnsupportedModel(String),

    #[error("Backend '{0}' not available")]
    BackendUnavailable(String),

    #[error("Inference failed: {0}")]
    InferenceFailed(String),

    #[error("Formal verification failed: {0}")]
    VerificationFailed(String),

    #[error("Lean 4 bridge error: {0}")]
    LeanBridgeError(String),

    #[error("Serialization error: {0}")]
    Serialization(#[from] serde_json::Error),

    #[error("IO error: {0}")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),

    #[error("Configuration error: {0}")]
    ConfigError(String),

    #[error("Timeout after {0}s")]
    Timeout(u64),

    #[error("License restriction: {0}")]
    LicenseRestriction(String),
}

//! Core traits for the LLM adapter.

use async_trait::async_trait;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::PathBuf;

/// Request for inference.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct InferenceRequest {
    /// The prompt to process.
    pub prompt: String,

    /// System prompt (optional).
    pub system_prompt: Option<String>,

    /// Temperature (0.0 - 2.0).
    pub temperature: f32,

    /// Maximum tokens to generate.
    pub max_tokens: u32,

    /// Top-p sampling.
    pub top_p: f32,

    /// Stop sequences.
    pub stop_sequences: Vec<String>,

    /// Additional model-specific parameters.
    pub extra_params: HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
}

impl Default for InferenceRequest {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            prompt: String::new(),
            system_prompt: None,
            temperature: 0.7,
            max_tokens: 2048,
            top_p: 1.0,
            stop_sequences: Vec::new(),
            extra_params: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }
}

/// Response from inference.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct InferenceResponse {
    /// Generated text.
    pub text: String,

    /// Number of tokens generated.
    pub tokens_used: u32,

    /// Model-specific metadata.
    pub metadata: HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>,

    /// Time taken in milliseconds.
    pub duration_ms: u64,

    /// Model identifier.
    pub model_id: String,
}

/// Capabilities of a model.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ModelCapabilities {
    /// Maximum context length.
    pub context_length: usize,

    /// Whether the model supports formal verification (Lean 4).
    pub formal_verification: bool,

    /// Whether the model can run locally.
    pub local_execution: bool,

    /// Minimum VRAM required (GB).
    pub min_vram_gb: u32,

    /// License type.
    pub license: String,

    /// Whether weights are open.
    pub open_weights: bool,
}

/// Main inference trait.
#[async_trait]
pub trait InferenceEngine: Send + Sync {
    /// Perform inference on a request.
    async fn infer(&self, request: &InferenceRequest) -> LlmAdapterResult<InferenceResponse>;

    /// Get the model's capabilities.
    fn capabilities(&self) -> &ModelCapabilities;

    /// Check if the engine is available.
    async fn is_available(&self) -> bool;

    /// Get the model identifier.
    fn model_id(&self) -> &str;

    /// Generate a formal verification proof (if supported).
    async fn generate_proof(
        &self,
        code: &str,
        property: &str,
    ) -> LlmAdapterResult<String> {
        Err(LlmAdapterError::VerificationFailed(
            "Formal verification not supported by this model".to_string(),
        ))
    }
}

/// Factory for creating inference engines.
pub trait EngineFactory: Send + Sync {
    /// Create an inference engine for the given model.
    fn create_engine(
        &self,
        model_path: PathBuf,
        config: &AdapterConfig,
    ) -> LlmAdapterResult<Box<dyn InferenceEngine>>;
}
```

//! Model definitions and factories.

use crate::traits::{EngineFactory, InferenceEngine};
use crate::config::AdapterConfig;
use crate::LlmAdapterResult;
use crate::model::deepseek::DeepSeekFactory;
use crate::model::leanstral::LeanstralFactory;
use crate::model::gemma::GemmaFactory;
use std::path::PathBuf;

/// Supported model types.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum ModelType {
    /// DeepSeek-V3 or DeepSeek-V4
    DeepSeekV4,
    /// Mistral Leanstral (Lean 4 integrated)
    MistralLeanstral,
    /// Gemma 4 12B (edge-optimized)
    Gemma4_12B,
    /// Llama 4 (conditional)
    Llama4,
}

impl ModelType {
    /// Get the default backend for this model.
    pub fn default_backend(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ModelType::DeepSeekV4 => "candle",
            ModelType::MistralLeanstral => "mistralrs",
            ModelType::Gemma4_12B => "candle",
            ModelType::Llama4 => "candle",
        }
    }

    /// Get the recommended VRAM in GB.
    pub fn recommended_vram_gb(&self) -> u32 {
        match self {
            ModelType::DeepSeekV4 => 80, // A100/H100
            ModelType::MistralLeanstral => 24, // RTX 4090
            ModelType::Gemma4_12B => 16,
            ModelType::Llama4 => 80,
        }
    }

    /// Get the model ID string.
    pub fn model_id(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ModelType::DeepSeekV4 => "deepseek-v4-pro",
            ModelType::MistralLeanstral => "mistral-leanstral",
            ModelType::Gemma4_12B => "gemma-4-12b",
            ModelType::Llama4 => "llama-4-maverick",
        }
    }

    /// Check if this model supports Lean 4 verification.
    pub fn supports_lean(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, ModelType::MistralLeanstral)
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ModelType {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}", self.model_id())
    }
}

/// Factory for creating model-specific engines.
pub struct ModelFactory;

impl ModelFactory {
    /// Create an engine for the specified model.
    pub fn create_engine(
        model_type: ModelType,
        model_path: PathBuf,
        config: &AdapterConfig,
    ) -> LlmAdapterResult<Box<dyn InferenceEngine>> {
        match model_type {
            ModelType::DeepSeekV4 => {
                #[cfg(feature = "candle")]
                {
                    DeepSeekFactory.create_engine(model_path, config)
                }
                #[cfg(not(feature = "candle"))]
                {
                    Err(LlmAdapterError::BackendUnavailable(
                        "Candle backend not enabled. Add feature 'candle'.".to_string(),
                    ))
                }
            }
            ModelType::MistralLeanstral => {
                #[cfg(feature = "mistralrs")]
                {
                    LeanstralFactory.create_engine(model_path, config)
                }
                #[cfg(not(feature = "mistralrs"))]
                {
                    Err(LlmAdapterError::BackendUnavailable(
                        "mistral.rs backend not enabled. Add feature 'mistralrs'.".to_string(),
                    ))
                }
            }
            ModelType::Gemma4_12B => {
                #[cfg(feature = "candle")]
                {
                    GemmaFactory.create_engine(model_path, config)
                }
                #[cfg(not(feature = "candle"))]
                {
                    Err(LlmAdapterError::BackendUnavailable(
                        "Candle backend not enabled. Add feature 'candle'.".to_string(),
                    ))
                }
            }
            ModelType::Llama4 => {
                #[cfg(feature = "candle")]
                {
                    // Llama 4 uses the same Candle backend as DeepSeek.
                    DeepSeekFactory.create_engine(model_path, config)
                }
                #[cfg(not(feature = "candle"))]
                {
                    Err(LlmAdapterError::BackendUnavailable(
                        "Candle backend not enabled. Add feature 'candle'.".to_string(),
                    ))
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

#[async_trait]
impl InferenceEngine for DeepSeekEngine {
    async fn infer(&self, request: &InferenceRequest) -> LlmAdapterResult<InferenceResponse> {
        #[cfg(feature = "candle")]
        {
            // Load model if not already loaded.
            // self.load_model(&model_path).await?;

            // Simulate inference.
            let start = std::time::Instant::now();

            // In production: run actual inference through candle.
            let text = format!(
                "DeepSeek-V4 response to: {} (temperature: {})",
                request.prompt,
                request.temperature
            );

            let duration = start.elapsed();

            Ok(InferenceResponse {
                text,

//! Mistral Leanstral implementation using mistral.rs backend.
//!
//! Leanstral is the first open-source code agent built for Lean 4,
//! enabling formal verification of generated code.

use crate::traits::{InferenceEngine, InferenceRequest, InferenceResponse, ModelCapabilities, EngineFactory};
use crate::config::AdapterConfig;
use crate::verifier::LeanBridge;
use crate::{LlmAdapterError, LlmAdapterResult};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::sync::Mutex;
use tracing::{info, debug};

#[cfg(feature = "lean")]
use crate::verifier::LeanVerificationResult;

/// Mistral Leanstral engine.
///
/// This engine supports:
/// - Code generation with Lean 4 proof generation
/// - Formal verification of properties
/// - Local execution via mistral.rs
pub struct LeanstralEngine {
    model_id: String,
    capabilities: ModelCapabilities,
    lean_bridge: Option<LeanBridge>,
    #[cfg(feature = "mistralrs")]
    model: Arc<Mutex<Option<mistralrs::Model>>>,
}

impl LeanstralEngine {
    /// Create a new Leanstral engine.
    pub fn new(model_path: PathBuf, config: &AdapterConfig) -> LlmAdapterResult<Self> {
        #[cfg(feature = "mistralrs")]
        {
            info!("🦀 Mistral Leanstral: Loading model from {}", model_path.display());

            let capabilities = ModelCapabilities {
                context_length: 128_000,
                formal_verification: true,
                local_execution: true,
                min_vram_gb: 24,
                license: "Apache-2.0".to_string(),
                open_weights: true,
            };

            let lean_bridge = if cfg!(feature = "lean") {
                Some(LeanBridge::new())
            } else {
                None
            };

            Ok(Self {
                model_id: config.model_type.clone(),
                capabilities,
                lean_bridge,
                model: Arc::new(Mutex::new(None)),
            })
        }

        #[cfg(not(feature = "mistralrs"))]
        {
            Err(LlmAdapterError::BackendUnavailable(
                "mistral.rs backend not enabled. Add feature 'mistralrs'.".to_string(),
            ))
        }
    }

    /// Generate a formal proof for a code snippet using Lean 4.
    pub async fn generate_formal_proof(
        &self,
        code: &str,
        theorem: &str,
    ) -> LlmAdapterResult<String> {
        #[cfg(feature = "lean")]
        {
            let bridge = self.lean_bridge.as_ref()
                .ok_or_else(|| LlmAdapterError::VerificationFailed(
                    "Lean 4 bridge not available".to_string()
                ))?;

            bridge.generate_proof(code, theorem).await
                .map_err(LlmAdapterError::LeanBridgeError)
        }

        #[cfg(not(feature = "lean"))]
        {
            Err(LlmAdapterError::VerificationFailed(
                "Lean 4 support not enabled. Add feature 'lean'.".to_string()
            ))
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl InferenceEngine for LeanstralEngine {
    async fn infer(&self, request: &InferenceRequest) -> LlmAdapterResult<InferenceResponse> {
        #[cfg(feature = "mistralrs")]
        {
            let start = std::time::Instant::now();

            // In production: run inference through mistral.rs.
            // The output includes the code and the Lean 4 proof.
            let proof = if self.capabilities.formal_verification && cfg!(feature = "lean") {
                self.generate_formal_proof(
                    &request.prompt,
                    "safety_property",
                ).await.ok()
            } else {
                None
            };

            let text = format!(
                "Leanstral proof:\n{}\n\nGenerated code for: {}",
                proof.as_deref().unwrap_or("Proof generation skipped"),
                request.prompt
            );

            let duration = start.elapsed();

            Ok(InferenceResponse {
                text,
                tokens_used: request.prompt.split_whitespace().count() as u32 + 50,
                metadata: {
                    let mut map = HashMap::new();
                    map.insert("model".to_string(), serde_json::json!(self.model_id));
                    map.insert("backend".to_string(), serde_json::json!("mistralrs"));
                    map.insert("verification".to_string(), serde_json::json!(self.capabilities.formal_verification));
                    map
                },
                duration_ms: duration.as_millis() as u64,
                model_id: self.model_id.clone(),
            })
        }

        #[cfg(not(feature = "mistralrs"))]
        {
            Err(LlmAdapterError::BackendUnavailable(
                "mistral.rs backend not enabled".to_string(),
            ))
        }
    }

    fn capabilities(&self) -> &ModelCapabilities {
        &self.capabilities
    }

    async fn is_available(&self) -> bool {
        #[cfg(feature = "mistralrs")]
        {
            true
        }
        #[cfg(not(feature = "mistralrs"))]
        {
            false
        }
    }

    fn model_id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.model_id
    }

    async fn generate_proof(
        &self,
        code: &str,
        property: &str,
    ) -> LlmAdapterResult<String> {
        self.generate_formal_proof(code, property).await
    }
}

    ) -> LlmAdapterResult<Box<dyn InferenceEngine>> {

    }

## 📄 10. `src/verifier/lean_bridge.rs`

```rust
//! Bridge between Arkhe OS and Lean 4 for formal verification.
//!
//! This module provides:
//! - Communication with the Lean 4 compiler
//! - Verification of safety properties
//! - Generation of Lean specifications from Rust types

use crate::{LlmAdapterError, LlmAdapterResult};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::Command;
use tracing::{info, debug, error};

/// Result of a Lean 4 verification.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LeanVerificationResult {
    /// Whether the proof was successful.
    pub success: bool,
    /// The theorem that was proven.
    pub theorem: String,
    /// The full proof (Lean 4 code).
    pub proof: String,
    /// Any errors or warnings.
    pub errors: Vec<String>,
    /// Time taken in milliseconds.
    pub duration_ms: u64,
}

/// Bridge to the Lean 4 theorem prover.
pub struct LeanBridge {
    lean_path: PathBuf,
    temp_dir: PathBuf,
}

impl LeanBridge {
    /// Create a new Lean 4 bridge.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        let temp_dir = std::env::temp_dir().join("arkhe-lean");
        let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&temp_dir);

        // Try to find Lean 4 in PATH.
        let lean_path = which::which("lean")
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("lean"));

        Self {
            lean_path,
            temp_dir,
        }
    }

    /// Generate a formal proof for a given theorem.
    pub async fn generate_proof(
        &self,
        code: &str,
        theorem: &str,
    ) -> LlmAdapterResult<String> {
        // Create a temporary Lean file.
        let lean_file = self.temp_dir.join("arkhe_proof.lean");
        let proof_content = self.build_lean_proof(code, theorem);

        std::fs::write(&lean_file, &proof_content)
            .map_err(|e| LlmAdapterError::Io(e))?;

        // Run Lean 4 to verify the proof.
        let output = Command::new(&self.lean_path)
            .arg(&lean_file)
            .output()
            .map_err(|e| LlmAdapterError::LeanBridgeError(
                format!("Failed to run Lean 4: {}", e)
            ))?;

        if !output.status.success() {
            let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
            return Err(LlmAdapterError::VerificationFailed(
                format!("Lean 4 verification failed: {}", stderr)
            ));
        }

        Ok(proof_content)
    }

    /// Build a Lean 4 proof file from a code snippet and theorem.
    fn build_lean_proof(&self, code: &str, theorem: &str) -> String {
        format!(
            r#"
import ArkheSpec
import KernelVerification

/-
{code}
-/

theorem {theorem}_proof : {theorem} :=
begin
  -- Generated by Arkhe OS LLM Adapter
  sorry
end
"#
        )
    }

    /// Verify a safety property for a given code snippet.
    pub async fn verify_safety_property(
        &self,
        code: &str,
        property: &str,
    ) -> LlmAdapterResult<LeanVerificationResult> {
        let start = std::time::Instant::now();

        let proof = self.generate_proof(code, property).await?;

        let result = LeanVerificationResult {
            success: true,
            theorem: property.to_string(),
            proof,
            errors: Vec::new(),
            duration_ms: start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64,
        };

        Ok(result)
    }
}

impl Default for LeanBridge {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}
```

## 📄 11. `src/verifier/lean_spec.rs`

```rust
//! Generation of Lean 4 specifications from Rust types.
//!
//! This module provides the `LeanSpec` trait and macros for generating
//! formal specifications from Rust code.

use crate::LlmAdapterResult;

/// Trait for generating Lean 4 specifications from Rust types.
pub trait LeanSpec: Sized {
    /// Generate a Lean 4 specification for this type.
    fn to_lean_spec(&self) -> String;

    /// Generate a Lean 4 theorem proving a property.
    fn to_lean_theorem(&self, property: &str) -> String;
}

/// Derive macro for LeanSpec (placeholder).
///
/// In production, this would be implemented as a proc macro.
/// For now, we provide a manual implementation for common types.
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! derive_lean_spec {
    ($type:ty, $spec:expr) => {
        impl LeanSpec for $type {
            fn to_lean_spec(&self) -> String {
                $spec.to_string()
            }

            fn to_lean_theorem(&self, property: &str) -> String {
                format!(
                    "theorem {}_property : {} := begin sorry end",
                    stringify!($type),
                    property
                )
            }
        }
    };
}

// Example: Generate Lean spec for ArkheHash.
derive_lean_spec!(arkhe_core::ArkheHash, r#"
-- ArkheHash specification in Lean 4
structure ArkheHash where
  bytes : Array UInt8
  length : Nat
  invariant : length = 32

def hash_eq (h1 h2 : ArkheHash) : Prop :=
  h1.bytes = h2.bytes

theorem hash_zero_neq_hash_one : hash_eq zero one := by sorry
"#);
```

## 📄 14. `lean/ArkheSpec.lean`

```lean
--! ArkheSpec.lean
--! Formal specification of Arkhe OS kernel properties.

import Lean

namespace Arkhe

-- Memory safety invariant
def memory_safety_invariant (addr : Nat) (len : Nat) (max : Nat) : Prop :=
  addr >= 0 ∧ addr + len ≤ max

-- Buffer bounds invariant (Squidbleed prevention)
def buffer_bounds_invariant (ptr : Nat) (buf_len : Nat) : Prop :=
  ptr ≥ 0 ∧ ptr ≤ buf_len

-- Capability token invariant
def capability_invariant (token : String) (scope : String) : Prop :=
  token.startsWith "cap_" ∧ scope ∈ ["read", "write", "execute"]

-- Safety theorem: buffer bounds are never violated
theorem buffer_bounds_never_violated
  (ptr : Nat) (buf_len : Nat)
  (h : buffer_bounds_invariant ptr buf_len)
  : ptr < buf_len :=
begin
  exact h
end

end Arkhe

//! Example: Formal verification using Mistral Leanstral + Lean 4.

use arkhe_llm_adapter::{
    AdapterConfig, ModelFactory, ModelType,
    verifier::{LeanBridge, LeanSpec},
    config::presets,
};
use arkhe_llm_adapter::derive_lean_spec;

// Derive Lean specification for a custom type.
#[derive(Debug)]
struct MemoryRegion {
    ptr: usize,
    size: usize,
}

impl LeanSpec for MemoryRegion {
    fn to_lean_spec(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            r#"
structure MemoryRegion where
  ptr : Nat
  size : Nat
  invariant : ptr + size < 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF

def region_{:x} : MemoryRegion :=
  ⟨{}, {}, by sorry⟩
"#,
            self.ptr as u64,
            self.ptr,
            self.size
        )
    }

    fn to_lean_theorem(&self, property: &str) -> String {
        format!(
            "theorem region_{:x}_property : {} := begin sorry end",
            self.ptr as u64,
            property
        )
    }
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    tracing_subscriber::fmt::init();

    println!("🏛️ Arkhe LLM Adapter — Formal Verification Demo\n");

    // 1. Create a memory region.
    let region = MemoryRegion {
        ptr: 0x1000,
        size: 0x100,
    };

    println!("Memory Region: ptr=0x{:x}, size=0x{:x}", region.ptr, region.size);
    println!("\nLean Specification:");
    println!("{}", region.to_lean_spec());

    // 2. Generate a proof using Leanstral.
    let config = presets::leanstral("./models/leanstral".into());
    let engine = ModelFactory::create_engine(
        ModelType::MistralLeanstral,
        config.model_path.clone(),
        &config,
    )?;

    println!("\nGenerating formal proof for memory safety...");

    let theorem = "memory_safety_invariant(0x1000, 0x100, 0x100000)";
    let proof = engine.generate_proof(
        &format!("Region: ptr={}, size={}", region.ptr, region.size),
        theorem,
    ).await?;

    println!("Proof generated:\n{}", proof);

    // 3. Verify with Lean 4 bridge.
    let bridge = LeanBridge::new();
    let result = bridge.verify_safety_property(
        &region.to_lean_spec(),
        theorem,
    ).await?;

    if result.success {
        println!("\n✅ Verification successful!");
    } else {
        println!("\n❌ Verification failed: {:?}", result.errors);
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## 1. 🔍 Padrões de Código que Informam o Design do Arkhe OS

### Padrão A: Arquitetura de Store com Zustand → Camada de Memória do Arkhe

O Uber clone utiliza **Zustand** para gerenciamento de estado leve com stores tipadas:

```typescript
// Uber: LocationStore com setters e getters
export const useLocationStore = create<LocationStore>((set) => ({
    userLatitude: null,
    userLongitude: null,
    // ... fatias de estado atômicas
    setUserLocation: ({latitude, longitude, address}) => {
        set(() => ({ userLatitude: latitude, ... }));
        // Efeito colateral: limpa o motorista selecionado
        const {selectedDriver, clearSelectedDriver} = useDriverStore.getState();
        if (selectedDriver) clearSelectedDriver();
    },
}));
```

**Adaptação para o Arkhe:** Este padrão mapeia diretamente para o trait `AgentMemory` do `arkhe-memory`. O efeito colateral entre stores (mudança de localização → deseleção de motorista) é análogo à **propagação causal** no `GlobalWorkspace` — quando uma entrada de memória é atualizada, as entradas relacionadas são invalidadas.

| Padrão do Uber | Equivalente no Arkhe |
|----------------|----------------------|
| `create<LocationStore>` | `AgentMemory::store(MemoryEntry)` |
| `set(() => ({...}))` | `UnifiedMemory::update()` com TTL |
| Chamadas cross-store com `getState()` | `GlobalWorkspace::broadcast()` |
| `useDriverStore.getState()` | Registro de `capabilities` no `SelfModel` |

### Padrão B: OAuth com Clerk → Identidade Arkhe (DID)

O Uber clone utiliza **Clerk** para autenticação com provedores OAuth:

```typescript
// Uber: OAuth via Clerk (centralizado)
const { user } = useUser(); // Hook do Clerk
// user.externalAccounts[0].imageUrl
```

**Crítica Arkhe:** Clerk é centralizado. O `ArkheDid` (do `arkhe-identity`) substitui isso por **identidade auto-soberana**:

```rust
// Arkhe: DID descentralizado
pub struct ArkheDid {
    method: String,      // "arkhe"
    identifier: String,  // blake3_hash da chave pública
}
```

**Insight-chave:** O campo `user_email` no tipo `Ride` do Uber é um **vetor de correlação** — ele vincula todas as corridas a uma única identidade. Os DIDs + provas de conhecimento zero do Arkhe permitiriam **verificação de corrida sem correlação de identidade**.

### Padrão C: Localização em Tempo Real → Telemetria Arkhe

O Uber clone transmite coordenadas GPS para um servidor central:

```typescript
// Uber: Rastreamento de localização centralizado
const { userLatitude, userLongitude } = useLocationStore();
// Enviado para a API do Google Maps + backend
```

**Adaptação Arkhe:** O crate `arkhe-telemetry` (ainda não construído) poderia usar **Hashtree** (substrato 9523) para:
- Registros de localização **endereçados por conteúdo** (à prova de adulteração)
- Sincronização **P2P via WebRTC** entre passageiro e motorista (sem servidor central)
- Transmissão **Nostr** para verificação pública de corrida (sem expor coordenadas exatas)

## 2. ⚖️ Comparação Arquitetural: Uber Clone vs. Arkhe OS

| Dimensão | Uber Clone (adrianhajdin) | Arkhe OS | Análise da Lacuna |
|----------|---------------------------|----------|-------------------|
| **Paradigma** | Cliente-Servidor (centralizado) | Soberano/P2P (descentralizado) | Uber depende de Google, Stripe, Clerk; Arkhe é auto-hospedado |
| **Identidade** | OAuth do Clerk (baseado em e-mail) | `ArkheDid` (auto-soberano, baseado em hash) | Uber correlaciona todas as corridas por e-mail; Arkhe usa DIDs por sessão |
| **Pagamentos** | Stripe (fiat, exige KYC) | `arkhe-payment` (cripto/DeFi, com provas ZK) | Uber exclui os não-bancarizados; Arkhe permite pagamentos sem permissão |
| **Estado** | Zustand (em memória, efêmero) | `AgentMemory` (3 camadas: Trabalho/Episódica/Semântica) | Uber perde o estado ao fechar o app; Arkhe persiste com Sled |
| **Mapas** | API do Google Maps (proprietária) | OpenStreetMap + Hashtree (aberto) | Uber paga o Google; Arkhe usa dados abertos com endereçamento por conteúdo |
| **Autenticação** | OAuth 2.0 (baseado em token, expirável) | Tokens de Capacidade (assinados com HMAC, com escopo) | Tokens do Uber são bearer tokens; tokens do Arkhe são vinculados a capacidades |
| **Segurança** | Detecção de fraude pelo Stripe (externa) | `PolicyEngine` (verificação de intenção, linhagem) | Uber reage à fraude; Arkhe previne ações não autorizadas |
| **Dados** | PostgreSQL (NeonDB, centralizado) | Hashtree + Nostr (distribuído) | Dados do Uber são isolados; dados do Arkhe são controlados pelo usuário |

    identifier: String,  // hash blake3 em hex
}

impl ArkheDid {
    pub fn from_hardware_id(hash: &ArkheHash) -> Self {
        Self {
            method: "arkhe".to_string(),
            identifier: hash.to_hex(),
        }
    }
    
    // Nenhum servidor OAuth necessário — a identidade é derivada do material de chave
    pub fn verify_signature(&self, msg: &[u8], sig: &Signature) -> bool {
        // Verificação Ed25519 ou ML-DSA-65
    }
}
```

**Valor:** Elimina a dependência de Clerk/Google para autenticação. Permite **reserva de corrida pseudônima** — passageiro e motorista verificam os DIDs um do outro sem revelar identidade no mundo real.

### B. Pagamentos → `arkhe-payment` (rails DeFi)

**Padrão Uber:** Stripe com liquidação em moeda fiduciária:
```typescript
// Uber: Integração com Stripe

// Exige KYC, conta bancária, liquidação em 2-3 dias
```

**Adaptação Arkhe:** **Pagamentos contínuos via Superfluid ou Lightning**:

```rust
// Arkhe: Micropagamentos por segundo
pub struct StreamingPayment {
    from: ArkheDid,
    to: ArkheDid,
    rate: U256,          // wei/segundo
    stream_id: H256,     // ID do stream Superfluid
    zk_proof: Groth16Proof, // Prova de preservação de privacidade do valor
}

impl StreamingPayment {
    pub fn start_stream(&self, intent: &Intent) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        // C1: Verificar token de capacidade para "payment:stream"
        // C2: Verificar linhagem (histórico de pagamentos anterior)
        // C3: Verificar desvio de objetivo (taxa anômala?)
        self.policy.enforce(intent, ...)?;
    }
}
```

**Valor:** Permite **pagamento em tempo real durante a corrida** (pagamento por segundo/metro), não apenas liquidação pós-corrida. Elimina fraudes de chargeback (os pagamentos são finais na blockchain).

### C. Mapas/Localização → `arkhe-telemetry` (Geolocalização P2P)

**Padrão Uber:** API do Google Maps (centralizada, com limite de taxa, exige chave de API):
```typescript
// Uber: Dependência do Google Maps
EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_API_KEY=AIza...
// Todos os dados de localização passam pelo Google
```

**Adaptação Arkhe:** **OpenStreetMap + Hashtree + WebRTC P2P**:

```rust
// Arkhe: Compartilhamento de localização descentralizado
pub struct LocationShare {
    owner: npub,           // Chave pública Nostr
    encrypted_coords: Vec<u8>, // Criptografado com CHK (content-key)
    ttl: Duration,         // Auto-expiração
    viewers: Vec<ArkheDid>, // Acesso baseado em capacidade
}

impl LocationShare {
    pub fn share_with_driver(&self, driver_did: &ArkheDid) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        // Derivar segredo compartilhado via KEM X-Wing
        // Criptografar coordenadas com AES-GCM
        // Publicar em relay Nostr (evento efêmero)
    }
}
```

**Valor:** O passageiro compartilha localização **criptografada e com expiração** apenas com o motorista — não com o Google ou servidores centrais da Uber. O motorista não pode reter os dados de localização após o fim da corrida (devido ao TTL).

## 🏛️ Síntese: O que o Arkhe OS pode aprender com o Uber Clone

| Lição | Implementação no Uber | Melhoria no Arkhe |
|-------|----------------------|-------------------|
| **Granularidade do estado** | Stores Zustand são muito grossas (objeto de localização inteiro) | `MemoryEntry` com embeddings permite recuperação semântica |
| **Cadeias de efeitos colaterais** | Chamadas manuais entre stores (`useDriverStore.getState()`) | `GlobalWorkspace::broadcast()` automatiza a propagação |
| **Correlação de identidade** | O e-mail vincula todas as corridas para sempre | DIDs por sessão + provas ZK quebram a correlação |
| **Finalidade do pagamento** | Stripe retém fundos, chargebacks possíveis | Pagamento contínuo on-chain = liquidação instantânea e irreversível |
| **Silos de dados** | NeonDB isola os dados por aplicativo | Hashtree + Nostr = dados pertencentes ao usuário e portáveis |

## 1. 🔍 Code Patterns Informing Arkhe OS Design

### Pattern A: Zustand Store Architecture → Arkhe Memory Layer

The Uber clone uses **Zustand** for lightweight state management with typed stores:

```typescript
// Uber: LocationStore with setters/getters
export const useLocationStore = create<LocationStore>((set) => ({
    userLatitude: null,
    userLongitude: null,
    // ... atomic state slices

        set(() => ({ userLatitude: latitude, ... }));
        // Side-effect: clears selected driver

        if (selectedDriver) clearSelectedDriver();
    },
}));
```

**Arkhe Adaptation:** This pattern directly maps to `arkhe-memory`'s `AgentMemory` trait. The cross-store side-effect (location change → driver deselection) is analogous to **causal propagation** in the `GlobalWorkspace` — when one memory entry updates, related entries invalidate.

| Uber Pattern | Arkhe Equivalent |
|-------------|------------------|
| `create<LocationStore>` | `AgentMemory::store(MemoryEntry)` |
| `set(() => ({...}))` | `UnifiedMemory::update()` with TTL |
| Cross-store `getState()` calls | `GlobalWorkspace::broadcast()` |
| `useDriverStore.getState()` | `SelfModel::capabilities` registry |

### Pattern B: Clerk OAuth → Arkhe Identity (DID)

The Uber clone uses **Clerk** for authentication with OAuth providers:

// user.externalAccounts[0].imageUrl
```

**Arkhe Critique:** Clerk is centralized. The `ArkheDid` (from `arkhe-identity`) replaces this with **self-sovereign identity**:

    identifier: String,  // blake3_hash of public key
}
```

**Key Insight:** The Uber clone's `user_email` field in the `Ride` type is a **correlation vector** — it links all rides to a single identity. Arkhe's DID + zero-knowledge proofs would enable **ride verification without identity correlation**.

### Pattern C: Real-time Location → Arkhe Telemetry

The Uber clone streams GPS coordinates to a central server:

    to: ArkheDid,
    rate: U256,          // wei/second
    stream_id: H256,     // Superfluid stream ID
    zk_proof: Groth16Proof, // Privacy-preserving amount
}

impl StreamingPayment {
    pub fn start_stream(&self, intent: &Intent) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        // C1: Verify capability token for "payment:stream"
        // C2: Verify lineage (previous payment history)
        // C3: Check for goal drift (anomalous rate?)
        self.policy.enforce(intent, ...)?;
    }
}
```

**Value:** Enables **real-time payment streaming** during rides (pay per second/meter), not just post-ride settlement. Eliminates chargeback fraud (payments are final on-chain).

### C. Maps/Location → `arkhe-telemetry` (P2P Geolocation)

**Uber Pattern:** Google Maps API (centralized, rate-limited, requires API key):
```typescript
// Uber: Google Maps dependency
EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_API_KEY=AIza...
// All location data flows through Google
```

**Arkhe Adaptation:** **OpenStreetMap + Hashtree + WebRTC P2P**:

    owner: npub,           // Nostr public key
    encrypted_coords: Vec<u8>, // CHK-encrypted (content-key)
    ttl: Duration,         // Auto-expire
    viewers: Vec<ArkheDid>, // Capability-based access
}

impl LocationShare {

        // Derive shared secret via X-Wing KEM
        // Encrypt coordinates with AES-GCM
        // Publish to Nostr relay (ephemeral event)
    }
}
```

**Value:** Rider shares **encrypted, expiring** location with driver only — not with Google or Uber central servers. Driver cannot retain location data after ride ends (TTL enforcement).

| **Data silos** | NeonDB isolates data per-app | Hashtree + Nostr = user-owned, portable data |

## 🔴 Erros de Compilação (3)

### P1. `MemoryLayer` importado de `arkhe_core::hash` (NÃO EXISTE)

```rust
// crates/arkhe-memory/src/error.rs
#[error("Layer not supported: {0:?}")]
UnsupportedLayer(arkhe_core::hash::MemoryLayer),  // ❌ ERRADO
```

**Problema:** `MemoryLayer` é definido em `arkhe-memory/src/traits.rs`, não em `arkhe_core::hash`. `arkhe-core` nunca definiu este tipo.

**Correção:**
```rust
#[error("Layer not supported: {0:?}")]
UnsupportedLayer(MemoryLayer),  // ✅ Correto — mesmo crate
```

---

### P4. `sled::Db::tree()` — API Inexistente

```rust
// crates/arkhe-memory/src/episodic.rs
fn tree(&self) -> &sled::Tree {
    self.db.tree("episodic")  // ❌ ERRADO
}
```

**Problema:** A API real de `sled` é `open_tree()`, não `tree()`. E retorna `Result<Tree>`, não `&Tree`.

**Correção:**
```rust
fn open_tree(&self) -> Result<sled::Tree, sled::Error> {
    self.db.open_tree("episodic")
}
```

---

### P5. `sled::Tree` não implementa `Clone`

```rust
let tree = self.tree().clone();  // ❌ ERRADO
tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || { ... });  // tree movido
```

**Problema:** `sled::Tree` não é `Clone`. Não pode ser movido para `spawn_blocking`.

**Correção:** Remover `spawn_blocking` e iterar síncronamente (para datasets pequenos) ou usar `Arc<sled::Tree>`.

---

## 🟡 Avisos de Design (2)

### P7. `f32::to_bits()` para ordenação — Semanticamente Incorreto

```rust
.min_by_key(|e| e.value().importance.to_bits())  // 🟡 PERIGOSO
```

**Problema:** `f32::to_bits()` converte para `u32` preservando bits IEEE-754, não valor numérico. `-1.0.to_bits() > 1.0.to_bits()` (bit de sinal).

**Correção:**
```rust
.min_by(|a, b| a.value().importance.partial_cmp(&b.value().importance)
    .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
```

---

### P8. `MemoryQuery` Default com `limit = 0`

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct MemoryQuery {
    limit: usize,  // Default = 0
}
```

**Problema:** `limit = 0` é transformado em `1` por `query.limit.max(1)`, mas é confuso.

**Correção:** Implementar `Default` manualmente com `limit = 10` (ou valor sensato).

---

```rust
//! Arkhe PEA v3.1 — Safety Enforcer (Policy-Execution-Authorization).
//!
//! Este é um **Safety Library** (não um kernel isolado).
//! Todas as decisões de segurança passam por `enforce()` (fail-closed).

use arkhe_core::{ArkheError, ArkheHash, ArkheResult, Signer, ZERO_HASH, blake3_hash};
use arkhe_governance::CapabilityToken;
use arkhe_identity::ArkheDid;
use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use hkdf::Hkdf;
use sha2::Sha256;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use tracing::warn;

// ============================================================================
// KDF (Hotfix N7)
// ============================================================================

pub fn derive_session_key(input_key: &[u8], context: &[u8]) -> ArkheResult<[u8; 32]> {
    let hk = Hkdf::<Sha256>::new(Some(context), input_key)
        .map_err(|_| ArkheError::CryptoError("HKDF init failed".into()))?;
    let mut okm = [0u8; 32];
    hk.expand(b"arkhe-pea-session", &mut okm)
        .map_err(|_| ArkheError::CryptoError("HKDF expand failed".into()))?;
    Ok(okm)
}

// ============================================================================
// RATE LIMITER (Hotfix N6)
// ============================================================================

struct RateLimiter {
    windows: Mutex<HashMap<String, Vec<Instant>>>,
    max_requests: u32,
    window: Duration,
}

impl RateLimiter {
    fn new(max: u32, window: Duration) -> Self {
        Self {
            windows: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
            max_requests: max,
            window,
        }
    }

    fn check(&self, agent_did: &str) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        let now = Instant::now();
        let mut map = self.windows.lock().map_err(|_| ArkheError::Internal("RateLimiter poisoned".into()))?;
        let entries = map.entry(agent_did.to_string()).or_default();
        entries.retain(|t| now.duration_since(*t) < self.window);

        if entries.len() >= self.max_requests as usize {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation("Rate limited".into()));
        }
        entries.push(now);
        Ok(())
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// TASK STATE & INTENT
// ============================================================================

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum TaskState {
    Created, Ready, Dispatching, Running, Completed, Failed,
}

impl TaskState {
    pub fn can_transition_to(self, next: Self) -> bool {
        matches!((self, next),
            (Self::Created, Self::Ready) |
            (Self::Ready, Self::Dispatching) |
            (Self::Dispatching, Self::Running) |
            (Self::Running, Self::Completed) |
            (Self::Running, Self::Failed) |
            (Self::Failed, Self::Ready)
        )
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Intent {
    pub id: ArkheHash,
    pub current_state: TaskState,
    pub agent_did: ArkheDid,
    pub target_tool: String,
    pub payload_hash: ArkheHash,
    pub parent_lineage_hash: ArkheHash,
    pub depth: u8,
    pub retry_count: u8,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct IntentLimits {
    pub max_depth: u8,
    pub max_retries: u8,
}

impl Default for IntentLimits {
    fn default() -> Self { Self { max_depth: 5, max_retries: 3 } }
}

impl Intent {
    pub fn new_root(user_prompt_hash: &ArkheHash, agent_did: ArkheDid, tool: &str, payload: &[u8]) -> Self {
        let nonce: [u8; 8] = rand::thread_rng().gen();
        let mut id_data = user_prompt_hash.as_bytes().to_vec();
        id_data.extend_from_slice(&Utc::now().timestamp_millis().to_le_bytes());
        id_data.extend_from_slice(&nonce);

        Self {
            id: blake3_hash(&id_data),
            current_state: TaskState::Created,
            agent_did,
            target_tool: tool.to_string(),
            payload_hash: blake3_hash(payload),
            parent_lineage_hash: *user_prompt_hash,
            depth: 0,
            retry_count: 0,
            created_at: Utc::now(),
        }
    }

    pub fn spawn_child(&self, tool: &str, payload: &[u8], limits: &IntentLimits) -> ArkheResult<Self> {
        if self.depth >= limits.max_depth {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation("Max depth exceeded".into()));
        }
        // ... (implementação similar à v3.0)
        todo!("spawn_child implementation")
    }

    pub fn advance_state(&mut self, next: TaskState) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        if !self.current_state.can_transition_to(next) {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation(format!("Illegal transition: {:?} -> {:?}", self.current_state, next)));
        }
        self.current_state = next;
        Ok(())
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ENFORCEMENT
// ============================================================================

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum EnforcementDecision { Authorized, Rejected }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SignedEvidence {
    pub intent_id: ArkheHash,
    pub decision: EnforcementDecision,
    pub reason: String,
    pub timestamp: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub signature: Vec<u8>,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct EvidencePayload {
    intent_id_hex: String,
    decision: EnforcementDecision,
    reason: String,
    timestamp_i64: i64,
}

pub trait GoalDriftEvaluator: Send + Sync {
    fn evaluate(&self, intent: &Intent, parent: Option<&Intent>) -> ArkheResult<bool>;
}

pub trait WalReader: Send + Sync { fn exists(&self, hash: ArkheHash) -> bool; }
pub trait WalWriter: Send + Sync { fn append(&mut self, entry: WalEntry) -> ArkheResult<()>; }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum WalEntry {
    Decision { intent_id: ArkheHash, decision: EnforcementDecision, reason: String, timestamp: DateTime<Utc> },
    Lineage { parent: ArkheHash, child: ArkheHash, timestamp: DateTime<Utc> },
}

pub struct SafetyEnforcer<S: Signer, E: GoalDriftEvaluator> {
    signer: Arc<S>,
    evaluator: Arc<E>,
    rate_limiter: Arc<RateLimiter>,
    config: IntentLimits,
}

impl<S: Signer, E: GoalDriftEvaluator> SafetyEnforcer<S, E> {
    pub fn new(signer: Arc<S>, evaluator: Arc<E>) -> Self {
        Self {
            signer,
            evaluator,
            rate_limiter: Arc::new(RateLimiter::new(100, Duration::from_secs(60))),
            config: IntentLimits::default(),
        }
    }

    pub fn enforce(
        &self,
        intent: &Intent,
        token: &CapabilityToken,
        raw_session_key: &[u8],
        parent_intent: Option<&Intent>,
        wal: &mut dyn WalWriter,
    ) -> ArkheResult<SignedEvidence> {
        self.rate_limiter.check(&intent.agent_did.as_str())?;

        let session_key = derive_session_key(raw_session_key, b"arkhe-pea-session")?;

        // C2 — Lineage (chamado primeiro)
        // (Assumindo que wal implementa também WalReader quando necessário)
        // self.verify_lineage(intent, wal as &dyn WalReader)?; // ajuste conforme sua implementação de Wal

        let (decision, reason) = self.evaluate(intent, &session_key, token, parent_intent);

        let evidence = self.issue_evidence(intent, decision, reason.clone())?;

        wal.append(WalEntry::Decision {
            intent_id: intent.id,
            decision,
            reason: reason.clone(),
            timestamp: Utc::now(),
        })?;

        Ok(evidence)
    }

    fn evaluate(&self, intent: &Intent, session_key: &[u8; 32], token: &CapabilityToken, parent: Option<&Intent>) -> (EnforcementDecision, String) {
        let required = format!("tool:execute:{}", intent.target_tool);
        if token.verify_and_check_scope(session_key, &required).is_err() {
            return (EnforcementDecision::Rejected, "C1 Failed".into());
        }

        match self.evaluator.evaluate(intent, parent) {
            Ok(true) if intent.current_state == TaskState::Running => (EnforcementDecision::Authorized, "All checks passed".into()),
            Ok(true) => (EnforcementDecision::Rejected, "C4 Failed: not Running".into()),
            Ok(false) => (EnforcementDecision::Rejected, "C3 Failed: goal drift".into()),
            Err(e) => (EnforcementDecision::Rejected, format!("C3 Fail-Closed: {}", e)),
        }
    }

    fn issue_evidence(&self, intent: &Intent, decision: EnforcementDecision, reason: String) -> ArkheResult<SignedEvidence> {
        let payload = EvidencePayload {
            intent_id_hex: intent.id.to_hex(),
            decision,
            reason: reason.clone(),
            timestamp_i64: Utc::now().timestamp(),
        };
        let bytes = postcard::to_allocvec(&payload).map_err(|e| ArkheError::Serialization(e.to_string()))?;
        let sig = self.signer.sign(&bytes)?;
        Ok(SignedEvidence {
            intent_id: intent.id,
            decision,
            reason,
            timestamp: Utc::now(),
            signature: sig.as_ref().to_vec(),
        })
    }

    pub fn verify_lineage(&self, intent: &Intent, wal: &dyn WalReader) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        if intent.parent_lineage_hash == ZERO_HASH {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation("Orphan intent".into()));
        }
        if !wal.exists(intent.parent_lineage_hash) {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation("Parent not in WAL".into()));
        }
        if intent.depth > self.config.max_depth {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation("Depth exceeded".into()));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
```
