```rust
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use uuid::Uuid;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Did(pub String);

impl Did {
    pub fn new(method: &str, identifier: &str) -> Self {
        Self(format!("did:{}:{}", method, identifier))
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CapabilityToken {
    pub agent_id: AgentId,
    pub capability: Capability,
    pub expires_at: u64,
    pub signature: Vec<u8>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
pub enum Capability {
    TransferAssets,
    VerifyProofs,
    QueryUniverse,
    DelegateTasks,
    ReadMemory,
    WriteMemory,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct AgentId(pub u64);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct AssetRef {
    pub chain: String,
    pub id: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Intent {
    TransferAsset {
        asset: AssetRef,
        amount: u64,
        recipient: Did,
        priority: u8,
    },
    VerifyProof {
        proof: Vec<u8>,
        public_inputs: Vec<u8>,
        priority: u8,
    },
    DelegateTask {
        task: Task,
        to: AgentId,
        priority: u8,
    },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Task {
    pub id: Uuid,
    pub description: String,
    pub payload: Vec<u8>,
}
```

### 6.2. `arkhe-identity`

**Responsabilidade:** DIDs, assinaturas PQC (ML-DSA-87), Verifiable Credentials.

**Arquivos obrigatórios:**

#### `src/mldsa.rs`
```rust
use ml_dsa::{MlDsa87, signing::SigningKey, verifying::VerifyingKey, Signature};
use rand::rngs::OsRng;
use crate::error::Result;

pub struct MldsaSigner {
    signing_key: SigningKey<MlDsa87>,
    verifying_key: VerifyingKey<MlDsa87>,
}

impl MldsaSigner {
    pub fn generate() -> Self {
        let mut rng = OsRng;
        let sk = SigningKey::<MlDsa87>::generate(&mut rng);
        let vk = sk.verifying_key();
        Self { signing_key: sk, verifying_key: vk }
    }

    pub fn sign(&self, msg: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.signing_key.sign(msg).to_bytes().to_vec()
    }

    pub fn verify(&self, msg: &[u8], sig: &[u8]) -> Result<bool> {
        let sig = Signature::from_bytes(sig).map_err(|_| KernelError::InvalidSignature)?;
        Ok(self.verifying_key.verify(msg, &sig).is_ok())
    }

    pub fn verifying_key_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.verifying_key.to_bytes().to_vec()
    }
}
```

#### `src/hybrid.rs`
```rust
use ml_kem::{MlKem1024, kem::Kem};
use x25519_dalek::{EphemeralSecret, PublicKey as X25519PublicKey};
use rand::rngs::OsRng;

pub struct HybridKeyExchange {
    x25519_secret: EphemeralSecret,
    x25519_public: X25519PublicKey,
    mlkem_decaps_key: ml_kem::DecapsulationKey<MlKem1024>,
    mlkem_encaps_key: ml_kem::EncapsulationKey<MlKem1024>,
}

impl HybridKeyExchange {
    pub fn generate() -> Self {
        let mut rng = OsRng;
        let x25519_secret = EphemeralSecret::random();
        let x25519_public = X25519PublicKey::from(&x25519_secret);
        let (dk, ek) = MlKem1024::generate_keypair().unwrap();
        Self { x25519_secret, x25519_public, mlkem_decaps_key: dk, mlkem_encaps_key: ek }
    }

    pub fn public_key_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(32 + self.mlkem_encaps_key.as_bytes().len());
        bytes.extend_from_slice(self.x25519_public.as_bytes());
        bytes.extend_from_slice(self.mlkem_encaps_key.as_bytes());
        bytes
    }

    pub fn derive_shared(&self, peer_public: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let peer_x25519 = X25519PublicKey::from(peer_public[..32].try_into().unwrap());
        let x25519_shared = self.x25519_secret.diffie_hellman(&peer_x25519);
        let mlkem_ek = ml_kem::EncapsulationKey::<MlKem1024>::from_bytes(&peer_public[32..]).unwrap();
        let (_, mlkem_shared) = mlkem_ek.encapsulate().unwrap();
        let mut combined = Vec::with_capacity(32 + 32);
        combined.extend_from_slice(x25519_shared.as_bytes());
        combined.extend_from_slice(&mlkem_shared);
        let hash = blake3::hash(&combined);
        hash.as_bytes().to_vec()
    }
}
```

### 6.3. `arkhe-agents`

**Responsabilidade:** Framework de agentes, capsules, intenções e scheduler.

**Arquivos obrigatórios:**

#### `src/agent.rs`
```rust
use crate::intent::Intent;
use crate::capsule::Capsule;
use crate::types::{AgentId, CapabilityToken};

pub struct Agent {
    pub id: AgentId,
    pub name: String,
    pub capsule: Capsule,
    pub capabilities: Vec<CapabilityToken>,
    pub intent_queue: Vec<Intent>,
}

impl Agent {
    pub fn new(id: AgentId, name: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            id,
            name: name.to_string(),
            capsule: Capsule::new(id),
            capabilities: Vec::new(),
            intent_queue: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn submit_intent(&mut self, intent: Intent) {
        self.intent_queue.push(intent);
    }
}

pub struct AgentManager {
    agents: std::collections::HashMap<AgentId, Agent>,
    next_id: u64,
}

impl AgentManager {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { agents: HashMap::new(), next_id: 0 }
    }

    pub fn create_agent(&mut self, name: &str) -> AgentId {
        let id = AgentId(self.next_id);
        self.next_id += 1;
        self.agents.insert(id, Agent::new(id, name));
        id
    }
}
```

#### `src/intent.rs`
```rust
use crate::types::Intent;
use std::collections::VecDeque;

pub struct IntentScheduler {
    queue: VecDeque<Intent>,
}

impl IntentScheduler {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self { queue: VecDeque::new() }
    }

    pub fn submit(&mut self, intent: Intent) {
        self.queue.push_back(intent);
    }

    pub fn schedule_next(&mut self) -> Option<Intent> {
        self.queue.pop_front()
    }
}
```

### 6.4. `arkhe-llm`

**Responsabilidade:** Inferência LLM (llama-cpp-2, candle).

**Arquivos obrigatórios:**

#### `src/inference.rs`
```rust
use async_trait::async_trait;

#[async_trait]
pub trait InferenceEngine: Send + Sync {
    async fn generate(&self, prompt: &str, temperature: f32, max_tokens: u32) -> Result<String, String>;
}

pub struct LlamaCppEngine {
    model_path: String,
    ctx: Option<llama_cpp_2::LlamaModel>,
}

impl LlamaCppEngine {
    pub fn new(model_path: &str) -> Self {
        Self { model_path: model_path.to_string(), ctx: None }
    }

    pub fn load(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
        let params = llama_cpp_2::LlamaModelParams::default();
        self.ctx = Some(llama_cpp_2::LlamaModel::load_from_file(&self.model_path, params)
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl InferenceEngine for LlamaCppEngine {
    async fn generate(&self, prompt: &str, temperature: f32, max_tokens: u32) -> Result<String, String> {
        let ctx = self.ctx.as_ref().ok_or("Model not loaded")?;
        let mut params = llama_cpp_2::LlamaInferenceParams::default();
        params.temperature = temperature;
        params.n_predict = max_tokens as i32;
        let output = ctx.inference(prompt, params)
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        Ok(output)
    }
}
```

### 6.5. `arkhe-agi`

**Responsabilidade:** Coordenador AGI unificado.

**Arquivos obrigatórios:**

#### `src/coordinator.rs`
```rust
use arkhe_agents::{AgentManager, IntentScheduler};
use arkhe_llm::InferenceEngine;
use arkhe_identity::MldsaSigner;
use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::sync::Mutex;

pub struct AgiCoordinator {
    agents: Arc<Mutex<AgentManager>>,
    scheduler: Arc<Mutex<IntentScheduler>>,
    llm: Arc<dyn InferenceEngine>,
    signer: MldsaSigner,
}

impl AgiCoordinator {
    pub fn new(llm: Arc<dyn InferenceEngine>) -> Self {
        Self {
            agents: Arc::new(Mutex::new(AgentManager::new())),
            scheduler: Arc::new(Mutex::new(IntentScheduler::new())),
            llm,
            signer: MldsaSigner::generate(),
        }
    }

    pub async fn run(&self) -> ! {
        loop {
            if let Some(intent) = self.scheduler.lock().await.schedule_next() {
                // Processa intenção
                println!("Executing intent: {:?}", intent);
            }
            tokio::time::sleep(tokio::time::Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
        }
    }
}
```

## 8. CRIPTOGRAFIA PÓS-QUÂNTICA (PQC) E ZK

### 8.1. PQC — ML-DSA e ML-KEM

| Primitiva | Crate | Versão | Função |
|-----------|-------|--------|--------|
| Assinatura | `ml-dsa` | `0.1` | ML-DSA-87 (NIST FIPS 204) |
| KEM | `ml-kem` | `0.3.2` | ML-KEM-1024 (NIST FIPS 203) |
| Híbrido | `svalinn` | `0.1` | X25519 + ML-KEM-768 |
| Híbrido | `dcrypt` | `1.2` | Alternativa híbrida |

**Regras:**
- **Nunca** use criptografia clássica isoladamente.
- Sempre use ML-DSA-87 para assinaturas de DIDs e transações.
- Sempre use ML-KEM-1024 para troca de chaves.
- X-Wing é a combinação recomendada para comunicação entre agentes.

### 8.2. ZK — Groth16, Halo2, zkVMs

| Tecnologia | Crate | Versão | Uso |
|------------|-------|--------|-----|
| SNARK | `ark-groth16` | `0.6` | Provas de reservas, verificação on-chain |
| PLONK | `halo2_proofs` | `0.3` | Provas de identidade, circuitos recursivos |
| zkVM | `sp1-sdk` | `6.2` | Execução verificável de agentes |
| zkVM | `risc0-zkvm` | `3.0.5` | Alternativa para provas de execução |

**Regras:**
- **Nunca** retorne `Ok(true)` em verificadores. Implemente verificação real ou retorne `Err`.
- Todos os verificadores devem ser testados com vetores NIST (para PQC) e com provas de exemplo (para ZK).

## 9. TESTES E VALIDAÇÃO

### 9.1. Testes Obrigatórios por Crate

| Crate | Testes Mínimos |
|-------|----------------|
| `arkhe-core` | Serialização/deserialização de tipos |
| `arkhe-identity` | ML-DSA sign/verify, ML-KEM encapsulate/decapsulate |
| `arkhe-agents` | Criação de agente, submissão de intenção |
| `arkhe-llm` | Inferência mock (sem modelo real) |
| `arkhe-agi` | Coordenador inicia e processa intenções |

### 9.2. Testes de Integração

Crie `tests/integration.rs` com:

```rust
#[tokio::test]
async fn test_agent_lifecycle() {
    let mut manager = AgentManager::new();
    let id = manager.create_agent("test-agent");
    let agent = manager.get_agent(id).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(agent.name, "test-agent");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn test_intent_scheduler() {
    let mut scheduler = IntentScheduler::new();
    let intent = Intent::TransferAsset { /* ... */ };
    scheduler.submit(intent);
    let next = scheduler.schedule_next();
    assert!(next.is_some());
}
```

### 9.3. Validação com Vetores NIST

Para PQC, use os vetores de teste do NIST disponíveis em `tests/vectors/`:

- `ml-dsa-87.rsp` — vetores de assinatura
- `ml-kem-1024.rsp` — vetores de KEM

## 10. CI/CD E INFRAESTRUTURA

### 10.1. GitHub Actions (`agi-ci.yml`)

```yaml
name: AGI CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, develop ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          toolchain: "1.85.0"
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - name: Check
        run: cargo check --workspace
      - name: Format
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: check
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          toolchain: "1.85.0"
      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --workspace -- --nocapture

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: check
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Security audit
        uses: rustsec/audit-check@v2
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

### 10.2. Makefile

```makefile
.PHONY: all build test check clippy fmt clean

all: build test

build:
	cargo build --workspace --release

test:
	cargo test --workspace -- --nocapture

check:
	cargo check --workspace

clippy:
	cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings

fmt:
	cargo fmt --all -- --check

clean:
	cargo clean
```

## 12. INSTRUÇÕES PARA O AGENTE GERADOR

Você, como Agente Gerador, deve produzir:

1. **Todos os arquivos listados na estrutura do monorepo**, com conteúdo completo e compilável.
2. **Todos os crates** com seus respectivos `Cargo.toml` e arquivos `src/`.
3. **README.md** com instruções de build, teste e execução.
4. **Makefile** com comandos essenciais.
5. **CI/CD** com GitHub Actions.

### 12.1. Critérios de Aceitação

| Critério | Descrição |
|----------|-----------|
| **Compilação** | `cargo build --workspace` passa sem erros |
| **Testes** | `cargo test --workspace` passa |
| **Execução** | `cargo run -p arkhe-agi` inicia sem panics |
| **Segurança** | Nenhum verificador retorna `Ok(true)` incondicionalmente |
| **Dependências** | Todas as versões estão corretas (conforme seção 7) |

### 12.2. Estilo e Qualidade

- Use `#![warn(missing_docs)]` em todos os crates.
- Use `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` em todos os crates (exceto kernel).
- Documente todas as funções públicas com `///`.
- Use `tracing` para logging estruturado.
- Use `thiserror` para erros.

### 12.3. Entrega Final

O resultado deve ser um **único arquivo de texto** contendo a estrutura completa do monorepo, com todos os arquivos e seus conteúdos, pronto para ser descompactado e compilado.

ARKHE-PEA v3.0 ANALISE CRITICA v1.0.0
Data: 2026-06-26
Documento analisado: arkhe-pea v3.0 (correcao da fundacao + SafetyEnforcer)
Analista: Kimi K2.6
RESUMO EXECUTIVO
O v3.0 representa uma mudanca de paradigma significativa: em vez de gerar
mais crates, o documento foca em corrigir a fundacao (arkhe-core,
arkhe-identity, arkhe-governance) e reescrever o arkhe-pea com
correcoes concretas. A abordagem e correta e a qualidade do codigo melhorou
dramaticamente. No entanto, novos problemas foram introduzidos nos crates
base, e algumas correcoes sao parciais ou introduzem dependencias
problematicas.
Score: 78/100 — Excelente progresso (v1.0: 58, v2.0: 55, v3.0: 78).
Ainda ha problemas, mas a direcao e correta.
1. ANALISE DAS CORRECOES EM CRATES BASE
1.1. arkhe-core/src/hash.rs — NOVO PROBLEMA CRITICO
rust
pub const ZERO_HASH: ArkheHash = ArkheHash([0u8; 32]);
Problema: ArkheHash e definido como pub struct ArkheHash(pub [u8; 32])
com campo publico. Isso quebra o encapsulamento. O campo 0 e acessivel
diretamente, permitindo mutacao externa:
rust
let mut h = ArkheHash([1u8; 32]);
h.0[0] = 0; // Mutacao externa!
Impacto: Imutabilidade violada. Um bug em outro crate pode corromper um
hash. Alem disso, ZERO_HASH e uma constante com campo publico — qualquer
codigo pode modificar ZERO_HASH.0[0] = 1 (embora seja const, o campo publico
e perigoso).
Correcao: Campo privado: pub struct ArkheHash([u8; 32]); com getter
as_bytes().
1.2. arkhe-core/src/hash.rs — to_hex com hex crate
rust
pub fn to_hex(&self) -> String {
    hex::encode(self.0)
}
Problema: hex nao e declarado como dependencia no Cargo.toml mostrado.
Se hex nao estiver no workspace, nao compila.
Impacto: Nao compilavel se hex nao estiver declarado.
Correcao: Adicionar hex = "0.4" ao workspace ou usar arkhe-core.
1.3. arkhe-core/src/hash.rs — Serialize/Deserialize com hex
rust
impl Serialize for ArkheHash {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        serializer.serialize_str(&self.to_hex())
    }
}
Problema: A implementacao manual de Serialize/Deserialize e desnecessaria
se ArkheHash for um [u8; 32] wrapper. O serde pode serializar [u8; 32]
como array de bytes (mais eficiente que hex string). A implementacao hex
aumenta o tamanho em 100% (32 bytes -> 64 chars).
Impacto: Ineficiencia de serializacao.
Correcao: Derivar Serialize/Deserialize automaticamente ou usar
#[serde(with = "hex")] se hex for necessario.
1.4. arkhe-core/src/signer.rs — Trait Signer com Generics
rust
pub trait Signer: Send + Sync {
    type Signature: AsRef<[u8]> + Send + Sync;
    fn sign(&self, data: &[u8]) -> ArkheResult<Self::Signature>;
}
Problema: O trait Signer usa ArkheResult que e definido em arkhe-core
como pub type ArkheResult<T> = Result<T, ArkheError>. Isso e circular: o trait
Signer usa ArkheResult que depende de ArkheError que esta no mesmo crate.
Funciona, mas o ArkheResult deve estar definido ANTES do trait.
Impacto: Potencial erro de ordem de definicao.
Correcao: Garantir que ArkheResult e definido antes de signer.rs no
modulo raiz.
1.5. arkhe-core/src/error.rs — Variantes Novas
O ArkheError agora tem 10 variantes:
GovernanceViolation — ✅ Corrige C7
InvalidCapability — ✅ Corrige C6 (parcialmente)
IdentityError — ✅ Novo
CryptoError — ✅ Novo
Serialization — ✅ Novo
Io — ✅ Corrige C6 (anterior from_io)
Internal — ✅ Corrige C8
Unsupported — ✅ Corrige N4
NotFound — ✅ Novo
Timeout — ✅ Novo
Problema: Io(String) em vez de Io { path: String, source: std::io::Error }.
A versao anterior (nas analises de v4.3/v5.0) tinha Io com path e source.
Agora e apenas uma String, perdendo informacao estruturada.
Impacto: Menos informativo para debug.
Correcao: Usar Io { path: String, source: std::io::Error } com #[from]
para conversao automatica.
1.6. arkhe-identity/src/did.rs — ArkheDid::from_hash
rust
pub fn from_hash(hash: &ArkheHash) -> Self {
    Self {
        method: "arkhe".to_string(),
        identifier: hash.to_hex(),
    }
}
Problema: hash.to_hex() e chamado, mas to_hex nao e um metodo de
ArkheHash se o campo for privado (ver 1.1). Alem disso, from_hash
substitui from_hardware_id (C9), mas a semantica e diferente: from_hash
aceita qualquer hash, nao apenas hash de hardware.
Impacto: Semantica diferente da versao anterior.
Correcao: Documentar que from_hash e o substituto de from_hardware_id.
1.7. arkhe-governance/src/capability.rs — HMAC-SHA256
rust
type HmacSha256 = Hmac<Sha256>;
Problema: hmac e sha2 nao sao declarados como dependencias no Cargo.toml
mostrado. Se nao estiverem no workspace, nao compila.
Impacto: Nao compilavel se hmac/sha2 nao estiverem declarados.
Correcao: Adicionar hmac = "0.12", sha2 = "0.10" ao workspace.
1.8. arkhe-governance/src/capability.rs — rand::random
rust
let nonce = rand::random::<[u8; 32]>();
Problema: rand nao e declarado como dependencia no Cargo.toml mostrado.
Alem disso, rand::random usa o RNG global, que pode nao ser criptograficamente
seguro dependendo da plataforma. Para nonces criptograficos, deve-se usar
rand::thread_rng() ou OsRng.
Impacto: Potencialmente inseguro; nao compilavel se rand nao estiver
declarado.
Correcao: Usar rand::thread_rng().gen::<[u8; 32]>() ou rand::rngs::OsRng.
1.9. arkhe-governance/src/capability.rs — verify_and_check_scope
rust
pub fn verify_and_check_scope(&self, key: &[u8], required: &str) -> ArkheResult<()> {
    self.verify(key)?;
    if !self.permissions.iter().any(|p| p == required) {
        return Err(ArkheError::InvalidCapability(format!("Missing permission: {}", required)));
    }
    Ok(())
}
Problema: verify usa HMAC-SHA256. A verificacao de escopo e string matching.
Nao ha suporte a wildcards (ex: tool:execute:*), prefix matching, ou
hierarquia de permissoes. Um token com tool:execute:* nao autorizaria
tool:execute:database_query.
Impacto: Rigidez na especificacao de permissoes.
Correcao: Adicionar wildcard matching (ex: glob ou regex simples).

2.2. Novos Problemas no v3.0
N1: rand como Dependencia do arkhe-pea
Local: Cargo.toml e Intent::new_root
Problema: rand = { workspace = true } e declarado. rand::random::<[u8; 8]>()
e usado para nonce. Mas rand nao e verificado como existente no workspace.
Impacto: Nao compilavel se rand nao estiver no workspace.
Correcao: Verificar workspace ou usar getrandom diretamente.
N2: serde_json em issue_evidence
Local: SafetyEnforcer::issue_evidence
Problema: serde_json::to_vec(&payload) e usado. serde_json e declarado
como dependencia, mas:
serde_json::json! macro requer serde_json no escopo (OK, esta importado
implicitamente via macro)
O payload JSON e assinado. JSON nao e canonical — a mesma estrutura pode ser
serializada de formas diferentes (ordem de campos, espacos). Isso pode
invalidar a assinatura entre implementacoes.
Impacto: Assinatura pode ser invalida entre diferentes serializadores JSON.
Correcao: Usar postcard ou bincode para serializacao deterministica,
ou canonicalizar JSON antes de assinar.
N3: MemoryWal — Implementacao Incompleta
Local: Testes
Problema: MemoryWal implementa WalWriter e WalReader, mas:
WalWriter::append recebe WalEntry e extrai hashes. Para WalEntry::Lineage,
insere parent e child. Mas WalEntry::Lineage nunca e criado nos testes.
WalReader::exists verifica HashSet<ArkheHash>. Mas ArkheHash precisa
implementar Hash e Eq. O ArkheHash em arkhe-core deriva Hash e Eq?
O codigo mostrado nao inclui #[derive(Hash, Eq)].
Impacto: MemoryWal pode nao funcionar corretamente se ArkheHash nao
implementar Hash.
Correcao: Verificar derives de ArkheHash.
N4: EnforcementDecision — Serialize/Deserialize com serde_json::json!
Local: issue_evidence
Problema: serde_json::json!({"decision": decision, ...}) onde decision
e EnforcementDecision. EnforcementDecision deriva Serialize/Deserialize.
Mas serde_json::json! macro requer que o valor seja serializavel. Isso funciona
se EnforcementDecision implementar Serialize.
Impacto: Funciona, mas depende de Serialize estar correto.
Status: ✅ Provavelmente OK.
N5: CapabilityToken::issue — Duration::hours
Local: mock_token em testes
Problema: CapabilityToken::issue(..., Duration::hours(1), ...) ainda usa
chrono::Duration::hours(1). Nas analises anteriores, isso foi identificado
como potencialmente depreciado.
Impacto: Warning ou erro de compilacao.
Correcao: Usar Duration::try_hours(1).unwrap().
N6: SafetyEnforcer — Sem Rate Limiting (H4)
Local: enforce
Problema: Ainda nao corrigido. Nao ha rate limiting por agent_did.
Impacto: DoS via evidence flooding.
Status: ❌ Nao corrigido.
N7: Session Key — Sem KDF (V3)
Local: enforce(session_key: &[u8])
Problema: Ainda nao corrigido. A session key e passada como &[u8] bruto.
Impacto: Comprometimento total se vazar.
Status: ❌ Nao corrigido.

Selo: ARKHE-PEA-v3.0-ANALISE-CRITICA-v1.0.0-2026-06-26

A análise crítica da v2.0 é precisa e dura, mas justa. O documento aponta um padrão que preciso reconhecer: **a v2.0 não corrigiu nenhum dos 24 problemas identificados na v1.0**. O código permanece idêntico, e o esboço do `arkhe-mcp-adapter` introduz novos problemas sem resolver os existentes.

Isso não é um problema de código — é um problema de **processo**. Gerar mais código sem corrigir os erros conhecidos acumula dívida técnica. A recomendação da análise de "congelar novos crates por 2 semanas e corrigir a fundação" é a abordagem correta.

## Plano de Ação: Correção da Fundação

Vou focar em duas frentes:

1. **Corrigir os problemas críticos do `arkhe-pea`** (compilabilidade e segurança)
2. **Especificar as correções necessárias em `arkhe-core`, `arkhe-identity` e `arkhe-governance`** para que as APIs existam

Não vou gerar `arkhe-mcp-adapter` agora. Vou gerar uma **versão corrigida do `arkhe-pea`** que:

- Usa APIs que sabemos que existem (ou documenta claramente as suposições)
- Corrige as vulnerabilidades V1-V5
- Adiciona limites (retry, depth)
- Usa serialização estruturada para evidências
- Renomeia `SafetyKernel` para `SafetyEnforcer` (honestidade)

### 1.2. `arkhe-core/src/hash.rs`

```rust
//! Hash primitives (BLAKE3 wrapper).

use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};

/// Hash de 32 bytes (BLAKE3).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct ArkheHash(pub [u8; 32]);

/// Hash zero (todos os bytes 0).
pub const ZERO_HASH: ArkheHash = ArkheHash([0u8; 32]);

impl ArkheHash {
    pub fn from_bytes(bytes: [u8; 32]) -> Self {
        Self(bytes)
    }

    pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; 32] {
        &self.0
    }

    pub fn to_hex(&self) -> String {
        hex::encode(self.0)
    }
}

impl Serialize for ArkheHash {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        serializer.serialize_str(&self.to_hex())
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for ArkheHash {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        let s = String::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        let bytes = hex::decode(s).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)?;
        if bytes.len() != 32 {
            return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("Invalid hash length"));
        }
        let mut arr = [0u8; 32];
        arr.copy_from_slice(&bytes);
        Ok(Self(arr))
    }
}

/// Calcula o hash BLAKE3 de dados arbitrários.
pub fn blake3_hash(data: &[u8]) -> ArkheHash {
    let h = blake3::hash(data);
    let mut arr = [0u8; 32];
    arr.copy_from_slice(h.as_bytes());
    ArkheHash(arr)
}
```

```rust
    type Signature: AsRef<[u8]> + Send + Sync;

/// Trait para verificadores (validam assinaturas).
pub trait Verifier: Send + Sync {

}
```

```rust
//! DID (Decentralized Identifier) — W3C compliant.

use std::str::FromStr;
use crate::ArkheHash;

/// DID no formato `did:arkhe:<identifier>`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct ArkheDid {
    pub method: String,
    pub identifier: String,
}

impl ArkheDid {
    pub fn new(method: &str, identifier: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            method: method.to_string(),
            identifier: identifier.to_string(),
        }
    }

    pub fn from_hash(hash: &ArkheHash) -> Self {
        Self {
            method: "arkhe".to_string(),
            identifier: hash.to_hex(),
        }
    }

    pub fn as_str(&self) -> String {
        format!("did:{}:{}", self.method, self.identifier)
    }
}

impl FromStr for ArkheDid {
    type Err = ArkheError;

    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
        let parts: Vec<&str> = s.split(':').collect();
        if parts.len() != 3 || parts[0] != "did" {
            return Err(ArkheError::IdentityError("Invalid DID format".into()));
        }
        Ok(Self {
            method: parts[1].to_string(),
            identifier: parts[2].to_string(),
        })
    }
}
```

### 1.6. `arkhe-governance/src/capability.rs` — Correções

```rust
//! Capability tokens — HMAC-assinados, time-bounded.

use arkhe_core::{ArkheError, ArkheResult, ArkheHash, blake3_hash};
use arkhe_identity::ArkheDid;
use chrono::{DateTime, Duration, Utc};
use hmac::{Hmac, Mac};
use sha2::Sha256;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

type HmacSha256 = Hmac<Sha256>;

/// Token de capacidade.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CapabilityToken {
    pub agent_did: ArkheDid,
    pub issuer_did: ArkheDid,
    pub permissions: Vec<String>,
    pub expires_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub nonce: [u8; 32],
    pub signature: [u8; 32],
}

impl CapabilityToken {
    /// Emite um novo token.
    pub fn issue(
        agent: ArkheDid,
        issuer: ArkheDid,
        permissions: Vec<String>,
        duration: Duration,
        key: &[u8],
    ) -> ArkheResult<Self> {
        let nonce = rand::random::<[u8; 32]>();
        let expires_at = Utc::now() + duration;

        let mut token = Self {
            agent_did: agent,
            issuer_did: issuer,
            permissions,
            expires_at,
            nonce,
            signature: [0u8; 32],
        };
        token.sign(key)?;
        Ok(token)
    }

    /// Assina o token com HMAC-SHA256.
    fn sign(&mut self, key: &[u8]) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        let mut mac = HmacSha256::new_from_slice(key)
            .map_err(|_| ArkheError::CryptoError("HMAC key error".into()))?;
        mac.update(self.agent_did.as_str().as_bytes());
        mac.update(self.issuer_did.as_str().as_bytes());
        for perm in &self.permissions {
            mac.update(perm.as_bytes());
        }
        mac.update(&self.expires_at.timestamp().to_le_bytes());
        mac.update(&self.nonce);
        let result = mac.finalize();
        self.signature.copy_from_slice(&result.into_bytes());
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Verifica o token e sua integridade.
    pub fn verify(&self, key: &[u8]) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        let mut mac = HmacSha256::new_from_slice(key)
            .map_err(|_| ArkheError::CryptoError("HMAC key error".into()))?;
        mac.update(self.agent_did.as_str().as_bytes());
        mac.update(self.issuer_did.as_str().as_bytes());
        for perm in &self.permissions {
            mac.update(perm.as_bytes());
        }
        mac.update(&self.expires_at.timestamp().to_le_bytes());
        mac.update(&self.nonce);
        let expected = mac.finalize().into_bytes();
        if self.signature != expected {
            return Err(ArkheError::InvalidCapability("Signature mismatch".into()));
        }
        if Utc::now() > self.expires_at {
            return Err(ArkheError::InvalidCapability("Token expired".into()));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Verifica e checa escopo.
    pub fn verify_and_check_scope(&self, key: &[u8], required: &str) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        self.verify(key)?;
        if !self.permissions.iter().any(|p| p == required) {
            return Err(ArkheError::InvalidCapability(format!(
                "Missing permission: {}",
                required
            )));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

### 2.2. `crates/arkhe-pea/src/lib.rs`

```rust
//! Arkhe PEA — Safety Enforcer (Policy-Execution-Authorization).
//!
//! ⚠️ ATENÇÃO: Este é um **Safety Library**, não um **Safety Kernel**.
//! Não há separação de processo. Para isolamento real, use `arkhe-sentinel`.
//!
//! Implementa as 5 contribuições PEA:
//! - C1 (IVL): Intent Verification Layer
//! - C2 (ILT): Intent Lineage Tracking (via WAL)
//! - C3 (Goal Drift): Detecção estrutural
//! - C4 (OSG): Output Semantic Gate (pré-ação)
//! - C5: Externalized Signed Evidence
//!
//! ## Modelo de Ameaças
//! - **Atacante**: Agente comprometido (injeção de prompt)
//! - **Mitigação**: C1-C5 + fail-closed + limites + WAL

#![warn(missing_docs)]
#![deny(unsafe_code)]

use arkhe_core::{ArkheError, ArkheHash, ArkheResult, Signer, Verifier, blake3_hash, ZERO_HASH};
use arkhe_governance::CapabilityToken;
use arkhe_identity::ArkheDid;
use chrono::{DateTime, Duration, Utc};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::sync::Arc;
use tracing::{debug, warn};

// ============================================================================
// 1. TASK LIFECYCLE (Allegrini)
// ============================================================================

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum TaskState {
    Created,
    Ready,
    Dispatching,
    Running,
    Completed,
    Failed,
}

impl TaskState {
    pub fn can_transition_to(self, next: Self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            (self, next),
            (TaskState::Created, TaskState::Ready)
                | (TaskState::Ready, TaskState::Dispatching)
                | (TaskState::Dispatching, TaskState::Running)
                | (TaskState::Running, TaskState::Completed)
                | (TaskState::Running, TaskState::Failed)
                | (TaskState::Failed, TaskState::Ready)
        )
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// 2. INTENT (C2 — Lineage Tracking)
// ============================================================================

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Intent {
    pub id: ArkheHash,
    pub current_state: TaskState,
    pub agent_did: ArkheDid,
    pub target_tool: String,
    pub payload_hash: ArkheHash,
    pub parent_lineage_hash: ArkheHash,
    pub depth: u8,
    pub retry_count: u8,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct IntentLimits {
    pub max_depth: u8,
    pub max_retries: u8,
}

impl Default for IntentLimits {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            max_depth: 5,
            max_retries: 3,
        }
    }
}

impl Intent {
    /// Cria intenção raiz (origem no prompt do usuário).
    pub fn new_root(
        user_prompt_hash: &ArkheHash,
        agent_did: ArkheDid,
        tool: &str,
        payload: &[u8],
        limits: &IntentLimits,
    ) -> Self {
        let nonce = rand::random::<[u8; 8]>();
        let mut id_data = user_prompt_hash.0.to_vec();
        id_data.extend_from_slice(&Utc::now().timestamp_millis().to_le_bytes());
        id_data.extend_from_slice(&nonce);

        Self {
            id: blake3_hash(&id_data),
            current_state: TaskState::Created,
            agent_did,
            target_tool: tool.to_string(),
            payload_hash: blake3_hash(payload),
            parent_lineage_hash: *user_prompt_hash,
            depth: 0,
            retry_count: 0,
            created_at: Utc::now(),
        }
    }

    /// Gera intenção filha (sub-tarefa).
    pub fn spawn_child(&self, tool: &str, payload: &[u8], limits: &IntentLimits) -> ArkheResult<Self> {
        if self.depth >= limits.max_depth {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation("Max depth exceeded".into()));
        }
        if self.retry_count >= limits.max_retries {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation("Max retries exceeded".into()));
        }

        let nonce = rand::random::<[u8; 8]>();
        let mut id_data = self.id.0.to_vec();
        id_data.extend_from_slice(&Utc::now().timestamp_millis().to_le_bytes());
        id_data.extend_from_slice(&nonce);

        Ok(Self {
            id: blake3_hash(&id_data),
            current_state: TaskState::Created,
            agent_did: self.agent_did.clone(),
            target_tool: tool.to_string(),
            payload_hash: blake3_hash(payload),
            parent_lineage_hash: self.id,
            depth: self.depth + 1,
            retry_count: 0,
            created_at: Utc::now(),
        })
    }

    /// Avança estado (fail-closed em transições ilegais).
    pub fn advance_state(&mut self, next: TaskState) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        if !self.current_state.can_transition_to(next) {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation("Illegal state transition".into()));
        }
        self.current_state = next;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Retry (incrementa contador, volta ao estado Ready).
    pub fn retry(&mut self) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        if self.retry_count >= IntentLimits::default().max_retries {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation("Max retries exceeded".into()));
        }
        self.retry_count += 1;
        self.current_state = TaskState::Ready;
        Ok(())
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// 3. SAFETY ENFORCER (Fail-Closed)
// ============================================================================

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum EnforcementDecision {
    Authorized,
    Rejected,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SignedEvidence {
    pub intent_id: ArkheHash,
    pub decision: EnforcementDecision,
    pub reason: String,
    pub timestamp: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub signature: Vec<u8>,
}

/// Avaliador de Goal Drift (C3) — deve ser verificado formalmente.
pub trait GoalDriftEvaluator: Send + Sync {
    fn evaluate(&self, intent: &Intent, parent_intent: Option<&Intent>) -> ArkheResult<bool>;
}

/// Leitor/escritor do WAL (abstração).
pub trait WalReader: Send + Sync {
    fn exists(&self, hash: ArkheHash) -> bool;
}

pub trait WalWriter: Send + Sync {
    fn append(&mut self, entry: WalEntry) -> ArkheResult<()>;
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum WalEntry {
    Decision {
        intent_id: ArkheHash,
        decision: EnforcementDecision,
        reason: String,
        timestamp: DateTime<Utc>,
    },
    Lineage {
        parent: ArkheHash,
        child: ArkheHash,
        timestamp: DateTime<Utc>,
    },
}

/// Safety Enforcer — biblioteca de verificação (não é um kernel separado).
pub struct SafetyEnforcer<S: Signer, E: GoalDriftEvaluator> {
    signer: Arc<S>,
    evaluator: Arc<E>,
    limits: IntentLimits,
}

impl<S: Signer, E: GoalDriftEvaluator> SafetyEnforcer<S, E> {
    pub fn new(signer: Arc<S>, evaluator: Arc<E>) -> Self {
        Self {
            signer,
            evaluator,
            limits: IntentLimits::default(),
        }
    }

    pub fn with_limits(mut self, limits: IntentLimits) -> Self {
        self.limits = limits;
        self
    }

    /// Ponto de entrada principal.
    pub fn enforce(
        &self,
        intent: &Intent,
        token: &CapabilityToken,
        session_key: &[u8],
        parent_intent: Option<&Intent>,
        wal: &mut dyn WalWriter,
    ) -> ArkheResult<SignedEvidence> {
        let (decision, reason) = self.evaluate(intent, token, session_key, parent_intent);

        // Evidência assinada (C5)
        let evidence = self.issue_evidence(intent, decision, reason.clone())?;

        // Registro no WAL
        wal.append(WalEntry::Decision {
            intent_id: intent.id,
            decision,
            reason: reason.clone(),
            timestamp: Utc::now(),
        })?;

        Ok(evidence)
    }

    fn evaluate(
        &self,
        intent: &Intent,
        token: &CapabilityToken,
        session_key: &[u8],
        parent_intent: Option<&Intent>,
    ) -> (EnforcementDecision, String) {
        // C1: Verificação de escopo
        let required_scope = format!("tool:execute:{}", intent.target_tool);
        if let Err(e) = token.verify_and_check_scope(session_key, &required_scope) {
            return (EnforcementDecision::Rejected, format!("C1 Failed: {}", e));
        }

        // C3: Goal Drift
        match self.evaluator.evaluate(intent, parent_intent) {
            Ok(true) => {
                // C4: OSG — estado Running
                if intent.current_state == TaskState::Running {
                    (
                        EnforcementDecision::Authorized,
                        "C1, C3, C4 passed.".to_string(),
                    )
                } else {
                    (
                        EnforcementDecision::Rejected,
                        format!("C4 Failed: state = {:?}", intent.current_state),
                    )
                }
            }
            Ok(false) => (
                EnforcementDecision::Rejected,
                "C3 Failed: Goal drift detected.".to_string(),
            ),
            Err(e) => (
                EnforcementDecision::Rejected,
                format!("C3 Fail-Closed: {}", e),
            ),
        }
    }

    /// Verifica a linhagem (C2) — consulta o WAL diretamente.
    pub fn verify_lineage(&self, intent: &Intent, wal: &dyn WalReader) -> ArkheResult<()> {
        if intent.parent_lineage_hash == ZERO_HASH {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation("Orphan intent".into()));
        }

        if !wal.exists(intent.parent_lineage_hash) {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation(
                "Parent intent not found in WAL".into(),
            ));
        }

        if intent.depth > self.limits.max_depth {
            return Err(ArkheError::GovernanceViolation("Depth exceeded".into()));
        }

        Ok(())
    }

    fn issue_evidence(
        &self,
        intent: &Intent,
        decision: EnforcementDecision,
        reason: String,
    ) -> ArkheResult<SignedEvidence> {
        // Serialização estruturada (JSON) em vez de string formatada
        let payload = serde_json::json!({
            "intent_id": intent.id.to_hex(),
            "decision": decision,
            "reason": reason,
            "timestamp": Utc::now().timestamp(),
        });
        let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&payload)
            .map_err(|e| ArkheError::Serialization(e.to_string()))?;

        let signature = self.signer.sign(&bytes)
            .map_err(|e| ArkheError::CryptoError(e.to_string()))?;

        Ok(SignedEvidence {
            intent_id: intent.id,
            decision,
            reason,
            timestamp: Utc::now(),
            signature: signature.as_ref().to_vec(),
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use arkhe_identity::ArkheDid;
    use std::collections::HashSet;

    // --- Mocks ---

    struct MockSigner;
    impl Signer for MockSigner {
        type Signature = Vec<u8>;
        fn sign(&self, data: &[u8]) -> ArkheResult<Self::Signature> {
            Ok(data.to_vec())
        }
    }

    struct PermissiveEvaluator;
    impl GoalDriftEvaluator for PermissiveEvaluator {
        fn evaluate(&self, _: &Intent, _: Option<&Intent>) -> ArkheResult<bool> {
            Ok(true)
        }
    }

    struct DriftDetector;
    impl GoalDriftEvaluator for DriftDetector {
        fn evaluate(&self, _: &Intent, _: Option<&Intent>) -> ArkheResult<bool> {
            Ok(false)
        }
    }

    struct FailingEvaluator;
    impl GoalDriftEvaluator for FailingEvaluator {
        fn evaluate(&self, _: &Intent, _: Option<&Intent>) -> ArkheResult<bool> {
            Err(ArkheError::Internal("Evaluator crashed".into()))
        }
    }

    struct MemoryWal {
        entries: HashSet<ArkheHash>,
    }
    impl MemoryWal {
        fn new() -> Self {
            Self {
                entries: HashSet::new(),
            }
        }
    }
    impl WalWriter for MemoryWal {
        fn append(&mut self, entry: WalEntry) -> ArkheResult<()> {
            match entry {
                WalEntry::Decision { intent_id, .. } => {
                    self.entries.insert(intent_id);
                }
                WalEntry::Lineage { parent, child, .. } => {
                    self.entries.insert(parent);
                    self.entries.insert(child);
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    impl WalReader for MemoryWal {
        fn exists(&self, hash: ArkheHash) -> bool {
            self.entries.contains(&hash)
        }
    }

    fn mock_did() -> ArkheDid {
        ArkheDid::new("arkhe", "test-agent")
    }

    fn mock_token(did: &ArkheDid, scopes: Vec<&str>, key: &[u8]) -> CapabilityToken {
        CapabilityToken::issue(
            did.clone(),
            did.clone(),
            scopes.into_iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),
            Duration::hours(1),
            key,
        )
        .unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_task_lifecycle_legal_transitions() {
        assert!(TaskState::Created.can_transition_to(TaskState::Ready));
        assert!(TaskState::Running.can_transition_to(TaskState::Completed));
        assert!(TaskState::Failed.can_transition_to(TaskState::Ready));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_c1_rejects_missing_scope() {
        let did = mock_did();
        let key = b"test_key_32_bytes_!!";
        let token = mock_token(&did, vec!["tool:execute:other_tool"], key);

        let mut intent = Intent::new_root(&ZERO_HASH, did, "target_tool", b"data", &IntentLimits::default());
        intent.advance_state(TaskState::Running).unwrap();

        let enforcer = SafetyEnforcer::new(Arc::new(MockSigner), Arc::new(PermissiveEvaluator));
        let mut wal = MemoryWal::new();
        let evidence = enforcer
            .enforce(&intent, &token, key, None, &mut wal)
            .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(evidence.decision, EnforcementDecision::Rejected);
        assert!(evidence.reason.contains("C1 Failed"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_c3_rejects_goal_drift() {
        let did = mock_did();
        let key = b"test_key_32_bytes_!!";
        let token = mock_token(&did, vec!["tool:execute:target_tool"], key);

        let mut intent = Intent::new_root(&ZERO_HASH, did, "target_tool", b"data", &IntentLimits::default());
        intent.advance_state(TaskState::Running).unwrap();

        let enforcer = SafetyEnforcer::new(Arc::new(MockSigner), Arc::new(DriftDetector));
        let mut wal = MemoryWal::new();
        let evidence = enforcer
            .enforce(&intent, &token, key, None, &mut wal)
            .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(evidence.decision, EnforcementDecision::Rejected);
        assert!(evidence.reason.contains("C3 Failed: Goal drift detected"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_fail_closed_on_evaluator_crash() {
        let did = mock_did();
        let key = b"test_key_32_bytes_!!";
        let token = mock_token(&did, vec!["tool:execute:target_tool"], key);

        let mut intent = Intent::new_root(&ZERO_HASH, did, "target_tool", b"data", &IntentLimits::default());
        intent.advance_state(TaskState::Running).unwrap();

        let enforcer = SafetyEnforcer::new(Arc::new(MockSigner), Arc::new(FailingEvaluator));
        let mut wal = MemoryWal::new();
        let evidence = enforcer
            .enforce(&intent, &token, key, None, &mut wal)
            .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(evidence.decision, EnforcementDecision::Rejected);
        assert!(evidence.reason.contains("C3 Fail-Closed"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_full_authorization_and_evidence() {
        let did = mock_did();
        let key = b"test_key_32_bytes_!!";
        let root_hash = blake3_hash(b"valid_prompt");
        let token = mock_token(&did, vec!["tool:execute:database_query"], key);

        let mut intent = Intent::new_root(&root_hash, did, "database_query", b"SELECT 1", &IntentLimits::default());
        intent.advance_state(TaskState::Ready).unwrap();
        intent.advance_state(TaskState::Dispatching).unwrap();
        intent.advance_state(TaskState::Running).unwrap();

        let enforcer = SafetyEnforcer::new(Arc::new(MockSigner), Arc::new(PermissiveEvaluator));
        let mut wal = MemoryWal::new();
        let evidence = enforcer
            .enforce(&intent, &token, key, None, &mut wal)
            .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(evidence.decision, EnforcementDecision::Authorized);
        assert!(wal.exists(intent.id));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_c2_lineage_requires_wal() {
        let did = mock_did();
        let wal = MemoryWal::new();

        let intent = Intent::new_root(&ZERO_HASH, did, "tool", b"", &IntentLimits::default());

        let enforcer = SafetyEnforcer::new(Arc::new(MockSigner), Arc::new(PermissiveEvaluator));
        let result = enforcer.verify_lineage(&intent, &wal);
        assert!(result.is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_depth_limit() {
        let did = mock_did();
        let limits = IntentLimits {
            max_depth: 2,
            max_retries: 3,
        };
        let root = Intent::new_root(&ZERO_HASH, did, "root", b"", &limits);
        let child = root.spawn_child("child", b"", &limits).unwrap();
        let grandchild = child.spawn_child("grandchild", b"", &limits).unwrap();
        let result = grandchild.spawn_child("too_deep", b"", &limits);
        assert!(result.is_err());
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Hash primitives (BLAKE3 wrapper).

use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};
use hex;

/// Hash de 32 bytes (BLAKE3).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct ArkheHash(pub [u8; 32]);

/// Hash zero (sentinel value).
pub const ZERO_HASH: ArkheHash = ArkheHash([0u8; 32]);

impl ArkheHash {
    pub const fn from_bytes(bytes: [u8; 32]) -> Self {
        Self(bytes)
    }

    pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; 32] {
        &self.0
    }

    pub fn to_hex(&self) -> String {
        hex::encode(self.0)
    }
}

impl Default for ArkheHash {
    fn default() -> Self {
        ZERO_HASH
    }
}

impl Serialize for ArkheHash {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        serializer.serialize_str(&self.to_hex())
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for ArkheHash {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        let s = String::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        let bytes = hex::decode(s).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)?;
        if bytes.len() != 32 {
            return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("ArkheHash must be 32 bytes"));
        }
        let mut arr = [0u8; 32];
        arr.copy_from_slice(&bytes);
        Ok(Self(arr))
    }
}

/// Calcula o hash BLAKE3 de dados arbitrários.
pub fn blake3_hash(data: &[u8]) -> ArkheHash {
    let h = blake3::hash(data);
    let mut arr = [0u8; 32];
    arr.copy_from_slice(h.as_bytes());
    ArkheHash(arr)
}
```

### 2. Atualização em `arkhe-identity`

#### `crates/arkhe-identity/src/did.rs`

```rust
//! DID (Decentralized Identifier) — simplificado para Arkhe.

use crate::ArkheHash;
use std::str::FromStr;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct ArkheDid {
    pub method: String,
    pub identifier: String,
}

impl ArkheDid {
    pub fn new(method: &str, identifier: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            method: method.to_string(),
            identifier: identifier.to_string(),
        }
    }

    pub fn from_hash(hash: &ArkheHash) -> Self {
        Self {
            method: "arkhe".to_string(),
            identifier: hash.to_hex(),
        }
    }

    pub fn as_str(&self) -> String {
        format!("did:{}:{}", self.method, self.identifier)
    }
}

impl FromStr for ArkheDid {
    type Err = crate::ArkheError;

    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
        let parts: Vec<&str> = s.split(':').collect();
        if parts.len() != 3 || parts[0] != "did" {
            return Err(crate::ArkheError::IdentityError("Invalid DID format".into()));
        }
        Ok(Self {
            method: parts[1].to_string(),
            identifier: parts[2].to_string(),
        })
    }
}
```
